questions.stem: Upon entering marriage, spouses incur __________.

options.A: legal and moral obligations to each other

questions.explanation: Marriage creates binding legal and moral obligations between spouses, including duties of care, support, and fidelity.

questions.stem: Marriage is best described as a __________.

options.A: permanent social union between recognized parties

questions.explanation: Marriage is understood as a lasting and permanent social union intended to endure over the lifetime of the partners.

questions.stem: One major institutional function of marriage is __________.

options.A: procreation and the legitimate raising of children

questions.explanation: A key function of marriage is procreation, legitimizing children and ensuring both biological and social family continuity.

questions.stem: Marriage provides a socially recognized context that helps in __________.
questions.explanation: Marriage regulates sexual behavior by providing a socially approved and legally recognized context for sexual relations.

questions.stem: By producing and socializing the next generation, marriage ensures __________.
questions.explanation: Marriage ensures the continuity of society by producing, legitimizing, and socializing the next generation.

questions.stem: By providing a stable environment for learning norms and values, marriage helps in __________.
questions.explanation: Marriage facilitates the socialization of children by providing a stable family environment for learning norms and values.

questions.stem: Marriage grants spouses __________.

options.A: specific legal rights and corresponding responsibilities

questions.explanation: Marriage confers specific legal rights on spouses and simultaneously imposes corresponding legal responsibilities.

questions.stem: By forming enduring family units, marriage promotes __________.
questions.explanation: Marriage contributes to social stability by forming enduring family units and orderly, recognized relationships.

questions.stem: By transmitting traditions, customs, and values across generations, marriage helps to __________.
questions.explanation: Marriage helps preserve culture by transmitting traditions, customs, and values from one generation to the next.

questions.stem: Marriage provides spouses with __________.

options.A: emotional and psychological support and companionship

questions.explanation: Marriage offers companionship and emotional support, contributing significantly to the mental and emotional well-being of spouses.

questions.stem: By establishing legally recognized partnerships, marriage helps regulate __________.

options.A: sexual relationships within accepted social boundaries

questions.explanation: Marriage regulates sexual relationships by establishing socially recognized and legally legitimate partnerships.

questions.stem: Monogamy is a form of marriage involving __________.
questions.explanation: Monogamy is the marriage of one man to one woman at a time.

questions.stem: Polygamy broadly refers to __________.

options.B: marriage between one man and one woman

questions.explanation: Polygamy is the practice of marrying multiple spouses - whether more than one wife or more than one husband.

questions.stem: Polygyny is the specific form of marriage in which __________.

options.A: one man is married to many women simultaneously
options.B: one woman is married to many men simultaneously
options.C: one man is married to one woman
options.D: many men are married to many women

questions.explanation: Polygyny is a form of polygamy in which one man has multiple wives at the same time.

questions.stem: Polyandry is the specific form of marriage in which __________.

options.A: one woman is married to many men simultaneously
options.B: one man is married to many women simultaneously
options.C: one man is married to one woman
options.D: a group of people all marry each other

questions.explanation: Polyandry is a form of polygamy in which one woman has multiple husbands at the same time.

questions.stem: The most common and widely legally recognized form of marriage globally is __________.
questions.explanation: Monogamy is the most widely practiced and legally recognized form of marriage across the world.

questions.stem: Polygamy can be broadly divided into which two main types?
questions.explanation: Polygamy is divided into two main types: polygyny (one man, many women) and polyandry (one woman, many men).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a recognized form of marriage?
questions.explanation: Democracy is a system of government, not a recognized form of marriage.

questions.stem: In many traditional African societies, the historically preferred and most common form of marriage was __________.
questions.explanation: Polygyny was historically the culturally preferred form of marriage in many traditional African societies.

questions.stem: The specific forms of marriage practiced in a society are primarily shaped by its __________.
questions.explanation: The forms of marriage practiced in a society are primarily shaped by its cultural norms, beliefs, and traditions.

questions.stem: The biological function of the family is primarily concerned with __________.

options.A: ensuring reproduction and the continuation of the species

questions.explanation: The biological function of the family is to ensure reproduction and the continuation of the human species.

questions.stem: The family's role in providing love, emotional support, and a sense of belonging is classified as its __________ function.
questions.explanation: Providing love and emotional support is a psychological function of the family, contributing to mental well-being of its members.

questions.stem: Which function of the family helps members acquire practical skills for economic survival?
questions.explanation: The economic function of the family helps members acquire skills and resources needed for economic survival.

questions.stem: The first and most fundamental agent of socialization for a child is the __________.
questions.explanation: The family is the primary and earliest agent of socialization, where a child first learns norms, values, and behaviors.

questions.stem: The process of passing culture, norms, and values from one generation to another is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Socialization is the process through which culture, norms, and values are transmitted from one generation to the next.

questions.stem: Which function of the family ensures that children learn the values, norms, and knowledge necessary for social life?
questions.explanation: The educational function of the family ensures that children learn values, norms, and knowledge necessary for social participation.

questions.stem: Family prestige in society is mainly linked to its __________.
questions.explanation: Family prestige is mainly linked to its social status, which reflects its social standing, honor, and reputation within the community.

questions.stem: The religious function of the family is primarily to __________.

options.A: promote the moral and spiritual growth of its members

questions.explanation: The religious function of the family is to promote the moral and spiritual development of all its members.

questions.stem: Which function of the family provides its members with relaxation, recreation, and enjoyment?
questions.explanation: The leisure function of the family provides relaxation, recreation, and enjoyment for its members.

questions.stem: A nuclear family consists of __________.

options.A: father, mother, and their children only

questions.explanation: A nuclear family is a basic family unit consisting of two parents (father and mother) and their children.

questions.stem: Which family type includes extended relatives such as grandparents, in-laws, uncles, and grandchildren?
questions.explanation: The extended family includes additional relatives beyond the nuclear unit, such as grandparents, in-laws, and grandchildren.

questions.stem: A family that is formed after one or both partners have remarried is known as a __________ family.
questions.explanation: A blended or remarriage family is formed when one or both partners bring children from previous relationships into the new marriage.

questions.stem: A family with only one parent present to raise the children is called a __________.
questions.explanation: A one-parent family, also called a single-parent family, is headed by only one parent raising the children.

questions.stem: Families where BOTH parents are employed in careers outside the home are known as __________ families.
questions.explanation: Dual-career families are those in which both parents are employed, often in professional or career-oriented positions.

questions.stem: A family consisting of an elderly couple aged 65 and above with no children at home is called an __________ family.
questions.explanation: An elderly family consists of an older couple, typically aged 65 and above, often living as an 'empty nest' household.

questions.stem: A family structure that includes three or more generations - parents, children, and grandparents - is known as a __________ family.
questions.explanation: A multigenerational family includes three or more generations, such as parents, children, and grandparents, living together or in close interaction.

questions.stem: A family unit formed by same-sex partners is known as a __________ family.
questions.explanation: A gay or lesbian family is formed by same-sex partners, with or without children.

questions.stem: A family that emerges as a result of migration, social change, and adaptation to new environments is called a __________ family.
questions.explanation: A transition family emerges as a result of migration and social change, adapting to new cultural and social environments.

questions.stem: In African society, marriage is mainly viewed as __________.

options.A: a family and community affair, not just a personal one
options.B: a purely personal matter between two individuals
options.D: an individual decision requiring no family input

questions.explanation: In African society, marriage is traditionally viewed as a family and community affair rather than solely a personal matter.

questions.stem: In traditional African societies, marriage involves the active participation of __________.
questions.explanation: Traditional African marriage involves the participation, negotiation, and consent of extended families from both sides.

questions.stem: One major purpose of marriage in African society is __________.
questions.explanation: Procreation is a central purpose of marriage in African society, ensuring lineage continuity and the family legacy.

questions.stem: The payment made by the groom's family to the bride's family as part of traditional African marriage negotiations is called __________.

options.B: Dowry paid by the bride's family

questions.explanation: Bride price is the payment (in cash, kind, or services) made by the groom's family to the bride's family.

questions.stem: Marriage in Nigerian society is primarily guided by __________.

options.A: the culture and tradition of the specific ethnic group

questions.explanation: Marriage in Nigerian society is primarily guided by the culture and traditions of the relevant ethnic group.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a recognized component of traditional African marriage?
questions.explanation: Court judgment is associated with statutory civil marriage, not traditional African marriage.

questions.stem: By formalizing unions and regulating social relationships, marriage helps to maintain __________.
questions.explanation: Marriage contributes to social stability by formalizing unions, creating recognized family structures, and regulating relationships.

questions.stem: Citizenship refers to __________.

options.A: the legal status of being a recognized member of a particular state
options.B: being a temporary visitor in a country

questions.explanation: Citizenship is the legal status that makes a person a recognized full member of a particular state or country.

questions.stem: A citizen is a person who __________.

options.A: is legally recognized as a full member of a state with rights and responsibilities
options.B: lives temporarily in a country as a visitor
options.C: has no legal rights in their country
options.D: is merely a resident without legal status

questions.explanation: A citizen is legally recognized as a full member of a state, with associated rights and responsibilities.

questions.stem: One primary way of acquiring citizenship is by __________.

options.A: birth to citizen parents or within the country's territory

questions.explanation: Citizenship can be acquired by birth - either by being born to citizen parents (jus sanguinis) or on the country's territory (jus soli).

questions.stem: Citizenship acquired automatically through birth is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Birthright citizenship is acquired automatically by being born to citizen parents or on a state's territory.

questions.stem: The legal process by which a foreigner can acquire citizenship of another country is called __________.
questions.explanation: Naturalization is a formal legal process by which a foreign national can voluntarily acquire citizenship of another country.

questions.stem: A key political right of citizens that distinguishes them from non-citizens is the right to __________.

options.A: vote and contest for public office

questions.explanation: A key political right of citizens is the right to vote in elections and to run for public office.

questions.stem: By creating a common legal bond and shared identity, citizenship promotes __________.
questions.explanation: Citizenship promotes national unity by creating a common legal bond and shared identity among all members of a state.

questions.stem: A person who is not a citizen of a country is legally referred to as a __________.
questions.explanation: A non-citizen is legally referred to as an alien or stranger within the context of a state's jurisdiction.

questions.stem: Citizenship confers on individuals both __________.
questions.explanation: Citizenship confers both rights (such as voting) and responsibilities (such as paying taxes and obeying laws).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor that WEAKENS nationalism and patriotism in a country?
questions.explanation: Poverty weakens nationalism and patriotism because widespread economic hardship leads to dissatisfaction and disengagement from national duties.

questions.stem: Illiteracy affects patriotism primarily because it __________.

options.A: limits awareness and the ability to participate in civic life

questions.explanation: Illiteracy limits a person's awareness of national issues and their ability to participate effectively in civic life.

questions.stem: Bad or oppressive government primarily leads to __________.

options.A: citizens losing trust in national institutions

questions.explanation: Oppressive government causes citizens to lose trust in national institutions, thereby weakening patriotism.

questions.stem: Negative peer group pressure may lead individuals to __________.

options.A: engage in anti-social and irresponsible behaviors

questions.explanation: Negative peer pressure can lead individuals to engage in anti-national or harmful behaviors that weaken patriotism.

questions.stem: The misuse of political power by leaders often results in __________.
questions.explanation: Misuse of political power typically leads to violence, injustice, and instability, undermining national loyalty.

questions.stem: The systematic deprivation of people's rights typically leads to __________.
questions.explanation: When people are deprived of their rights, it often results in social unrest, protest, and civil disobedience.

questions.stem: The underdevelopment of rural areas typically causes __________.
questions.explanation: Rural underdevelopment leads to migration to cities and increases economic and social inequality across regions.

questions.stem: High levels of unemployment in a society contribute to __________.

options.A: social vices, crime, and widespread dissatisfaction

questions.explanation: Unemployment breeds frustration, social vices, crime, and general dissatisfaction, reducing citizens' commitment to the nation.

questions.stem: One major effect of factors like poverty and oppressive governance is that citizens become __________.

options.A: less committed to their national duties and obligations

questions.explanation: Factors like poverty and oppression make citizens less willing to fulfill their responsibilities and duties to the nation.

questions.stem: Patriotism is most fundamentally shown through __________.

options.A: genuine love for and active commitment to one's country

questions.explanation: Patriotism is fundamentally demonstrated by genuine love for and active commitment to one's country.

questions.stem: A citizen paying their taxes as and when due is a direct example of __________.
questions.explanation: Paying taxes is a civic duty that demonstrates patriotism by contributing to national development.

questions.stem: Showing loyalty and obedience to legitimate authority demonstrates __________.
questions.explanation: Loyalty and obedience to legitimate authority are acts of patriotism that uphold the rule of law and national stability.

questions.stem: Participating in elections by casting one's vote is a form of __________.
questions.explanation: Voting is a patriotic act of civic participation that strengthens democracy and national governance.

questions.stem: Willingness to defend the nation, whether in a military or civilian capacity, shows __________.
questions.explanation: Defending the nation in any capacity - military or civilian - is a direct manifestation of patriotism.

questions.stem: Showing respect for national symbols such as the flag and national anthem reflects __________.
questions.explanation: Showing respect for national symbols like the flag and anthem is a visible expression of patriotism and national pride.

questions.stem: Assisting law enforcement agents in fighting crime is an act of __________.
questions.explanation: Assisting law enforcement in combating crime is a patriotic act that contributes to national security and social order.

questions.stem: The duty to uphold and defend the constitution belongs to __________.

options.A: every citizen, not just leaders or officials

questions.explanation: Upholding the constitution is a civic duty expected of every citizen as an expression of patriotism.

questions.stem: Refusing to participate in illegal strikes that harm the national economy is an act of __________.
questions.explanation: Refusing to participate in illegal strikes demonstrates respect for the law and commitment to national stability.

questions.stem: The River Niger, from which Nigeria derives its name, is approximately __________ kilometres in length.
questions.explanation: The River Niger is approximately 4,180 kilometres in length, making it the third-longest river in Africa.

questions.stem: The significant annual masquerade festival celebrated by the Ebira people to honor their heritage and mark the end of the lunar year is called __________.
questions.explanation: The Ekuechi Festival is a major traditional masquerade celebration of the Ebira people of Kogi State.

questions.stem: Among the Ebira people, when a male child is born at home, his face is traditionally dusted with a white clay or powder known as __________.
questions.explanation: In traditional Ebira custom, Itutu refers to the symbolic white powder used in the reception ritual for a newborn male child.

questions.stem: Among the Ebira people, when a female child is born, the traditional welcome powder used is called __________.
questions.explanation: Ahito is the traditional powder or ash preparation used in the infant reception ceremonies for a newborn female child in Ebira culture.

questions.stem: The first Kanuri Empire came to an end following a devastating war with the __________ people.
questions.explanation: The first Kanuri Empire collapsed after a destructive series of wars with the Bulala people.

questions.stem: In Kanuri society, the Magira refers to __________.

options.A: the Queen Mother or elder sister of the king (Mai)
options.B: the eldest son of the king
options.D: the head of the Kanuri military

questions.explanation: Among the Kanuri, the Magira is the title given to the Queen Mother or the elder sister of the king (known as the Mai).

questions.stem: The Kanuri saying 'Even a flawed ruler is better than having no leadership at all' reflects which cultural value?

options.A: The irreplaceable importance of governance and order
options.B: The absolute power of the military
options.C: The rejection of all forms of leadership
options.D: The preference for anarchy over bad governance

questions.explanation: This proverb expresses that even an imperfect ruler is preferable to having no ruler and no governance structure.

questions.stem: The Yoruba traditional facial mark consisting of three short horizontal lines on the cheeks is called __________.
questions.explanation: Pele refers to a very common traditional Yoruba facial mark made up of three short horizontal lines cut on the cheeks.

questions.stem: The Yoruba traditional facial mark consisting of parallel vertical lines placed on the cheeks is called __________.
questions.explanation: Abaja is a traditional Yoruba facial marking configuration characterized by parallel vertical stripes or blocks on the cheeks.

questions.stem: Among the Edo people, the symbol 'Osun Oba Ado' represents __________.

options.A: the mystical power and divine authority of the Oba of Benin
options.C: the war god of the Edo people

questions.explanation: Osun Oba Ado is an Edo symbol that embodies the mystical power and divine authority of the Oba of Benin.

questions.stem: The River Niger bisects the Igbo homeland in Southern Nigeria, with the larger portion of Igbo territory situated to the __________ of the river.
questions.explanation: The River Niger bisects the Igbo homeland, and the larger portion of Igbo territory lies to the east of the river.

questions.stem: The African philosophical statement 'I am, because we are; and since we are, therefore I am' primarily expresses which core value?

options.A: The communal nature of identity - personhood is rooted in community
options.B: Individualism and personal achievement above all
options.C: The supremacy of the Supreme Being over humanity

questions.explanation: This Ubuntu philosophy expresses that an individual's identity and existence is inseparable from the community they belong to.

questions.stem: A family structure in which multiple generations - grandparents, parents, and children - live together or closely interact is called an __________ family.
questions.explanation: An extended family structure links multiple generations together, going beyond the basic nuclear family layout.

questions.stem: A large family system composed entirely of blood relatives living communally together is called a __________ family.
questions.explanation: A consanguine family is a large family system made up entirely of blood relatives who live communally together.

questions.stem: A family where one parent is absent due to death, separation, or divorce is called a __________ family.
questions.explanation: A broken family is one where one parent is absent due to death, separation, or divorce, leaving the remaining parent to manage the household.

questions.stem: A marriage conducted according to ethnic and cultural practices, involving bride price and family consent, is called __________.
questions.explanation: Traditional or customary marriage is conducted in accordance with the ethnic and cultural practices of a people.

questions.stem: A marriage conducted within a religious institution - either Christian or Islamic - is called __________.
questions.explanation: Religious marriage is a union conducted within a religious institution, such as a church (Christian) or a mosque (Islamic ceremony).

questions.stem: A marriage that is a legally recognized union registered with the government under the constitution is called __________.
questions.explanation: Court marriage is a statutory union legally registered with the government and recognized under the constitution.

questions.stem: The legal dissolution of a marriage, granted by a court after fulfilling required legal conditions, is called __________.
questions.explanation: Divorce is the formal legal process of dissolving a marriage through a court after all required conditions have been met.

questions.stem: A situation where a couple lives apart but remains legally married is called __________.
questions.explanation: Separation occurs when a couple lives apart without legally dissolving the marriage; they may or may not later reconcile.

questions.stem: The Edo (Benin) people refer to the Supreme Being as __________.
questions.explanation: The Edo people of Benin call the Supreme Being Osanobua (also referred to as Osa-Nriagene or Osa-Nevbuwa).

questions.stem: The Igala people refer to the Supreme Being as __________.
questions.explanation: The Igala people use the name Ojo to refer to the Supreme Being.

questions.stem: The Nupe people refer to the Supreme Being as __________.
questions.explanation: The Nupe people call their Supreme Being Soko.

questions.stem: The Efik and Ibibio peoples refer to the Supreme Being as __________.
questions.explanation: The Efik and Ibibio peoples use the name Abasi to refer to the Supreme Being.

questions.stem: Another name by which the Ijaw people refer to the Supreme Being is __________.
questions.explanation: The Ijaw people call the Supreme Being Tamuno (also Ayamaowei or Temearau) in addition to Egbesu.

questions.stem: The Urhobo people refer to the Supreme Being as __________.
questions.explanation: The Urhobo people use the name Oghere to refer to the Supreme Being.

questions.stem: Arts and crafts involving leather works in Nigeria are predominantly associated with __________.
questions.explanation: Kano is the primary centre in Nigeria associated with the traditional production of arts and crafts involving leather works.

questions.stem: The traditional craft of pottery in Nigeria is predominantly associated with __________.
questions.explanation: Pottery as a traditional craft is predominantly associated with Ilorin, Uyo, and Ifo in Nigeria.

questions.stem: In addition to Benin, brass and bronze work as a traditional craft is also significantly associated with __________.
questions.explanation: Brass and bronze work is prominently associated with Benin, Kano, and Awka in traditional Nigerian craftsmanship.

questions.stem: In addition to Oyo (Iseyin), traditional weaving in Nigeria is also prominently associated with __________.
questions.explanation: Traditional weaving is famously associated with Oyo (Iseyin for Aso-Ofi) and Kano (Rimi) in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Hausa term used to refer specifically to the nomadic, pastoral, bush-dwelling Fulani is __________.
questions.explanation: Fulanin Daji literally translates to 'Bush Fulani', denoting the semi-nomadic and fully nomadic pastoral cattle herders.

questions.stem: Among the Ebira people, a male child painted with Itutu is believed to be either an Ekere or an Omoziere. An Omoziere is a child believed to be __________.

options.A: born with a special mission or purpose

questions.explanation: Among the Ebira, Omoziere refers to a child believed to have been born with a specific mission or purpose in life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is TRUE regarding culture and its relationship to human beings?

options.A: Culture is restricted to human beings alone
options.B: Culture is found equally in humans and animals
options.C: Animals are equally capable of creating culture
options.D: Culture is inherited naturally like instinct

questions.explanation: Culture is unique to human beings because it requires language, structured learning, and complex social interaction for its transmission.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the largest ethnic group in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Hausa-Fulani ethnic group is the largest in Nigeria, primarily concentrated in the northern part of the country.

questions.stem: Nigeria is often referred to as the 'Giant of Africa' primarily because of __________.

options.A: its combination of the largest population, significant economy, and vast landmass
options.B: its dominance in continental politics alone
options.D: its leadership in African cultural arts

questions.explanation: Nigeria is the Giant of Africa due to its largest population, relatively large economy, and one of the largest landmasses on the continent.

questions.stem: The official language used in government, education, and business in Nigeria is __________.
questions.explanation: English is Nigeria's official language, used in government, education, and business - a legacy of British colonialism.

questions.stem: The capital city of Nigeria since 1991 is __________.
questions.explanation: Abuja has been the federal capital of Nigeria since 1991, replacing Lagos.

questions.stem: The dominant religion in Northern Nigeria is __________.
questions.explanation: Islam is the predominant religion in Northern Nigeria.

questions.stem: The festival of Eid-el-Fitr, which marks the end of Ramadan, is associated with which religion?
questions.explanation: Eid-el-Fitr is a major Islamic festival that marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan.

questions.stem: Nigeria gained independence from British colonial rule on October 1, __________.
questions.explanation: Nigeria gained its independence from Britain on October 1, 1960.

questions.stem: The Nok civilization, known for its distinctive terracotta sculptures, flourished in what is now the area around __________.
questions.explanation: The Nok culture flourished in the area around the Jos Plateau in present-day Plateau State.

questions.stem: Chinua Achebe, the acclaimed author of 'Things Fall Apart', belongs to which Nigerian ethnic group?
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe was an Igbo writer born in Ogidi, Anambra State.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a traditional Yoruba dance form?
questions.explanation: Bata is a traditional Yoruba drum-driven dance form from southwestern Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Ooni of Ife, one of Nigeria's most respected traditional rulers, is based in which state?
questions.explanation: The Ooni of Ife is the traditional ruler of Ile-Ife, which is located in Osun State.

questions.stem: Nigeria's film industry, Nollywood, is widely regarded as the __________ largest film industry in the world by volume of production.
questions.explanation: Nollywood is the second-largest film industry in the world by volume of production, after Bollywood of India.

questions.stem: In West African folklore, Anansi is typically depicted as a __________.
questions.explanation: Anansi is a popular trickster spider character in West African and African-Caribbean folklore.

questions.stem: The traditional flowing robe commonly worn by Yoruba men on formal occasions is called __________.
questions.explanation: Agbada is the flowing wide-sleeved robe commonly worn by Yoruba men on formal and ceremonial occasions.

questions.stem: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria is primarily known for __________.
questions.explanation: The Niger Delta is Nigeria's main oil-producing region, containing the country's largest oil reserves.

questions.stem: Who is widely considered the father of modern Nigerian art?
questions.explanation: Ben Enwonwu (Bennie) is widely regarded as the father of modern Nigerian art.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian city is famous for its ancient walls and gates known as the 'Ganuwa'?
questions.explanation: The Kano City walls and gates (Ganuwa) are famous historical landmarks that date back centuries.

questions.stem: The traditional martial sport known as 'Dambe' is primarily associated with which Nigerian ethnic group?
questions.explanation: Dambe is a traditional Hausa martial art/boxing sport, particularly popular in northern Nigeria.

questions.stem: Nigeria's first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, was from which Nigerian ethnic group?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe (Zik of Africa) was an Igbo nationalist and Nigeria's first ceremonial President.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian writer became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986?
questions.explanation: Prof. Wole Soyinka became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986.

questions.stem: In Yoruba cosmology, Osun is the goddess associated with __________.
questions.explanation: Osun is the Yoruba goddess associated with fertility, love, beauty, and freshwater rivers.

questions.stem: The traditional Igbo wrestling festival is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Kokawa is a traditional Igbo wrestling festival celebrating athleticism and cultural heritage.

questions.stem: Nigeria's highest mountain, Chappal Waddi, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Chappal Waddi, Nigeria's highest peak at 2,419m, is located in the Gashaka Gumti National Park in Taraba State.

questions.stem: The Benin Kingdom is most famous historically for its __________.
questions.explanation: The Benin Kingdom is renowned worldwide for its sophisticated brass and bronze sculptural art.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a traditional Igbo masquerade?
questions.explanation: Mmanwu is a prominent traditional Igbo masquerade representing ancestral spirits.

questions.stem: The official currency of Nigeria is the __________.
questions.explanation: The Naira (₦) is the official currency of Nigeria, introduced in 1973.

questions.stem: Which river serves as part of the international boundary between Nigeria and Cameroon?
questions.explanation: The Cross River forms part of the international boundary between Nigeria and Cameroon.

questions.stem: The famous Osogbo School of art is based in the town of __________.
questions.explanation: The Osogbo Art School is a famous contemporary art movement based in Osogbo, Osun State.

questions.stem: Traditional Hausa architecture is most characteristically built with __________.
questions.explanation: Traditional Hausa architecture prominently features mud-brick construction with intricate decorative designs.

questions.stem: The Igbo 'New Yam Festival' (Iri Ji) is primarily celebrated to __________.

options.A: mark the beginning of the yam harvest season
options.B: mark the end of the planting season

questions.explanation: The New Yam Festival (Iri Ji) is celebrated to mark the beginning of the yam harvest and give thanks for the harvest.

questions.stem: Femi Kuti, the son of Fela Kuti, is a prominent musician known for playing __________.
questions.explanation: Femi Kuti continues his father Fela's legacy as a prominent Afrobeat musician and activist.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method used to foster national integration in Nigeria?

options.D: Limiting interaction between different ethnic groups

questions.explanation: The NYSC scheme was established to foster national unity and integration by posting graduates to states other than their state of origin.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian ethnic group is predominantly found in the Niger Delta region?
questions.explanation: The Ijaw (Izon) people are the largest ethnic group predominantly inhabiting the Niger Delta region of Nigeria.

questions.stem: The term 'Nigerianization' refers to __________.

options.B: The gradual replacement of foreigners in positions of leadership by Nigerians
options.C: The ban on all foreign cultures

questions.explanation: Nigerianization refers to the post-independence policy of replacing expatriates and foreign nationals in key leadership and professional positions with qualified Nigerians.

questions.stem: Aso Villa, the seat of power in Nigeria, is located in __________.
questions.explanation: Aso Rock Villa is the official residence and primary workplace of the President of Nigeria, located in Abuja.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian ethnic group is associated with the famous 'Igba Nkwu' marriage ceremony?
questions.explanation: Igba Nkwu (wine-carrying ceremony) is the traditional Igbo marriage ceremony in which the bride searches for her groom in a crowd and offers him palm wine.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian leader was instrumental in establishing the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)?
questions.explanation: The NYSC scheme was established by General Yakubu Gowon in 1973, following the Nigerian Civil War, to promote national unity and reconstruction.

questions.stem: The House of Representatives in Nigeria is part of the __________.
questions.explanation: The House of Representatives, together with the Senate, forms the National Assembly - the legislative branch of the Nigerian government.

questions.stem: The practice of multiculturalism in Nigeria emphasizes __________.

options.C: The recognition and respect of diverse cultures

questions.explanation: Multiculturalism promotes the coexistence, recognition, and equal respect of Nigeria's many diverse cultural identities.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Constitution recognizes approximately how many ethnic groups?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is home to over 250 ethnic groups, making it one of the most ethnically diverse nations in the world.

questions.stem: Which ethnic group is predominantly associated with the Igaldung Festival?
questions.explanation: The Igaldung Festival is a major cultural festival associated with the Tiv people of Benue State.

questions.stem: Which ethnic group is known for the Ekpe masquerade society?
questions.explanation: The Ekpe (Leopard) masquerade society is a powerful secret society and cultural institution of the Efik and related Cross River peoples.

questions.stem: Which festival celebrated by the Yoruba marks the beginning of a new year?
questions.explanation: The Olojo Festival, celebrated in Ile-Ife, marks the creation of the world and the beginning of a new cycle - it is one of the most sacred Yoruba festivals.

questions.stem: The Waza Festival is popularly associated with which ethnic group?
questions.explanation: The Waza Festival is a cultural celebration associated with the Kanuri people of northeastern Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which state is famous for the Argungu Fishing Festival?
questions.explanation: The Argungu International Fishing and Cultural Festival is held annually in Argungu, Kebbi State, and is one of Nigeria's most internationally recognized cultural events.

questions.stem: Which ethnic group is associated with the ancient Nok Culture?
questions.explanation: The Nok Culture is named after the village of Nok in present-day Kaduna State, and is associated with the ancient Nok people whose terracotta sculptures are among Africa's earliest known art forms.

questions.stem: Which city is famous for the Olojo Festival?
questions.explanation: The Olojo Festival is celebrated in Ile-Ife, Osun State - the ancestral home of the Yoruba people - in honor of Ogun, the god of iron.

questions.stem: Which of the following foods is traditionally associated with the Yoruba people?
questions.explanation: Moi Moi (steamed bean pudding) is a popular traditional Yoruba dish made from blended peeled beans, peppers, and spices.

questions.stem: Which ethnic group practices the Nnobi traditional rituals?
questions.explanation: The Nnobi are an Igbo community in Anambra State known for distinct traditional rituals and cultural practices documented by scholars like Ifi Amadiume.

questions.stem: Which constitution was in use in Nigeria during the colonial period beginning in 1922?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution was introduced in 1922 during British colonial rule in Nigeria. It expanded legislative representation and marked an important stage in Nigeria's constitutional development.

questions.stem: In what year was the Clifford Constitution introduced in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution was introduced in 1922 by Governor Hugh Clifford and became a significant constitutional framework during the colonial era.

questions.stem: In what year was the Macpherson Constitution introduced in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution was introduced in 1951. It allowed for greater Nigerian participation in governance and laid the foundation for federalism in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Who was responsible for introducing the Clifford Constitution in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was introduced by Governor Hugh Clifford and represented an important constitutional reform during British colonial administration.

questions.stem: Which of the following constitutions immediately preceded the Macpherson Constitution in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 preceded the Macpherson Constitution of 1951 and was replaced due to criticism and demands for broader participation by Nigerians.

questions.stem: Which of the following constitutions immediately preceded the Clifford Constitution in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Lugard Constitution of 1914, established following the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria, preceded the Clifford Constitution of 1922 and laid the foundation for Nigeria's constitutional development.

questions.stem: Which constitution governed Nigeria during the colonial era beginning in 1922?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution, introduced in 1922 by Governor Hugh Clifford, was a major colonial constitution that governed Nigeria during an important period of British colonial administration.

questions.stem: The introduction of which constitution in 1922 marked a significant constitutional development during British colonial rule in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution was introduced in 1922 and represented a significant step in Nigeria's constitutional history under British colonial administration.

questions.stem: Which pair of Nigerian leaders died while serving in office rather than being assassinated?

options.A: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa and Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi
options.C: Sani Abacha and Umaru Musa Yar'Adua
options.D: Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi and Umaru Musa Yar'Adua

questions.explanation: Both Sani Abacha and Umaru Musa Yar'Adua died while serving in office, whereas the others listed were assassinated.

questions.stem: Which of the following leaders was assassinated earliest in Nigerian history?
questions.explanation: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was killed during the January 1966 coup, making him the earliest among the listed leaders to be assassinated.

questions.stem: Who wrote the Nigerian National Pledge?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Pledge was written by Felicia Adebola Adeyoyin and was adopted as part of efforts to promote patriotism among Nigerian citizens.

questions.stem: In what year was the Nigerian National Pledge introduced?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Pledge was introduced in 1976 as part of national orientation and unity initiatives following the civil war era.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian Head of Government was killed during the January 1966 military coup?
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria's first and only Prime Minister, was killed during the military coup of January 1966.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian military Head of State was assassinated in July 1966?
questions.explanation: General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi was assassinated during the counter-coup of July 1966, which led to major political changes in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian Head of State was assassinated in February 1976?
questions.explanation: General Murtala Muhammed was assassinated on 13 February 1976 during an attempted military coup in Lagos.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian Head of State died in office in June 1998?
questions.explanation: General Sani Abacha died while serving as Nigeria's Head of State in June 1998.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian President died in office in May 2010?
questions.explanation: President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua died in office on 5 May 2010, after a prolonged illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following Nigerian leaders was not assassinated but died while in office?
questions.explanation: Unlike the others listed, Sani Abacha was not assassinated; he died while serving as Head of State in 1998.

questions.stem: General Murtala Muhammed was assassinated while travelling to work in Lagos, which was part of which region of Nigeria at the time?
questions.explanation: General Murtala Muhammed was assassinated in Lagos on 13 February 1976. Lagos was historically located in Nigeria's Western Region before the creation of additional states and geopolitical zones.

questions.stem: In which city was General Murtala Muhammed assassinated on 13 February 1976?
questions.explanation: General Murtala Muhammed was assassinated in Lagos during an attempted coup on 13 February 1976 while travelling to his office.

questions.stem: What is the official name of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's full official name is the Federal Republic of Nigeria, reflecting its federal structure and republican system of government.

questions.stem: When did Nigeria officially become a Federal Republic?
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a Federal Republic on October 1, 1963, exactly three years after independence, replacing the Queen as Head of State with a Nigerian President.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the three tiers of government in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal, State, and Local Government Areas

questions.explanation: Nigeria operates three tiers of government: the Federal (central) government, State governments, and Local Government Areas (LGAs).

questions.stem: How many states does Nigeria currently have?
questions.explanation: Nigeria currently has 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, making 37 administrative units in total.

questions.stem: When was Abuja designated as Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory?
questions.explanation: Abuja was designated as the Federal Capital Territory in 1976 under General Murtala Muhammed's regime, though it officially became the functioning capital in 1991 under General Ibrahim Babangida.

questions.stem: Which city served as Nigeria's capital before Abuja?
questions.explanation: Lagos was Nigeria's capital city from independence in 1960 until 1991 when Abuja officially became the seat of government.

questions.stem: What are the three arms of the Nigerian Federal Government?
questions.explanation: The three arms of Nigeria's federal government are the Executive (President), the Legislature (National Assembly), and the Judiciary (Courts).

questions.stem: How many members make up the Nigerian Senate?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Senate has 109 members - three senators representing each of the 36 states, plus one senator for the FCT Abuja.

questions.stem: How many members make up the Nigerian House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian House of Representatives, the lower chamber of the National Assembly, has 360 members.

questions.stem: How many senators does each state send to the Nigerian Senate?
questions.explanation: Each of Nigeria's 36 states is represented by 3 senators in the Senate, with an additional senator for the FCT Abuja, totalling 109.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of Nigeria's six geopolitical zones?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's six geopolitical zones are: North-West, North-East, North-Central, South-West, South-East, and South-South. 'South-Central' does not exist.

questions.stem: What is the supreme law of Nigeria?

options.B: The 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution (as amended) is the supreme law of Nigeria, and any law inconsistent with it is void to the extent of its inconsistency.

questions.stem: When did Nigeria's current (1999) constitution take effect?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution came into force on May 29, 1999, the same day President Olusegun Obasanjo was inaugurated, marking the start of the Fourth Republic.

questions.stem: What is May 29 officially known as in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: May 29 is officially Democracy Day in Nigeria, commemorating the return to civilian rule in 1999 when President Obasanjo was inaugurated.

questions.stem: What type of government system does Nigeria operate?
questions.explanation: Nigeria operates a Federal Presidential system in which the President is both the Head of State and Head of Government, modelled after the United States system.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of INEC in Nigeria?

options.B: Organising, undertaking, and supervising all elections in Nigeria

questions.explanation: INEC (Independent National Electoral Commission) is constitutionally mandated to organise, undertake, and supervise all elections at the federal and state levels in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which court is the highest in Nigeria's judicial hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is the apex court and final court of appeal in the Nigerian judicial system.

questions.stem: What document formally merged Northern and Southern Nigeria in 1914?
questions.explanation: The Amalgamation Proclamation of January 1, 1914, signed by Lord Frederick Lugard, merged the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria with the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.

questions.stem: Who was the first Governor-General of amalgamated Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard was the first Governor-General of amalgamated Nigeria, serving from 1914 to 1919 after overseeing the unification.

questions.stem: Which two entities were merged to form Nigeria in 1914?

options.A: The Colony of Lagos and the Niger Delta Protectorate
options.B: The Protectorate of Northern Nigeria and the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria
options.D: The Royal Niger Company territories and the Lagos Colony

questions.explanation: The 1914 amalgamation merged the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria with the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria under Lord Lugard.

questions.stem: What was the first formal constitution introduced in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922, named after Governor Sir Hugh Clifford, was the first formal constitution introduced in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What major democratic principle did the Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduce for the first time?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced the elective principle for the first time in Nigeria, allowing four elected members (three from Lagos, one from Calabar) to sit on the Legislative Council.

questions.stem: Which constitution introduced regionalism by dividing Nigeria into North, West, and East?
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946, introduced by Governor Sir Arthur Richards, divided Nigeria into three regions - North, West, and East - thereby introducing regionalism.

questions.stem: Why was the Richards Constitution of 1946 heavily criticised by Nigerian nationalists?

options.B: It was imposed without consulting Nigerians
options.D: It introduced the presidential system prematurely

questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution was criticised primarily because it was imposed without adequate consultation with Nigerians, unlike later constitutions that involved broader participation.

questions.stem: Which constitution is noted as the first to be drafted with wide Nigerian participation?
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was notable for being the first Nigerian constitution drafted after wide consultations with Nigerians at all levels of society.

questions.stem: Which constitution established Nigeria as a Federation and introduced the federal system of government?
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 (also called the Federal Constitution) established Nigeria as a federation with a clear division of powers between the federal and regional governments.

questions.stem: Which constitution was in place when Nigeria gained independence on October 1, 1960?
questions.explanation: The Independence Constitution of 1960 granted full political independence to Nigeria on October 1, 1960, while still retaining the British Queen as Head of State.

questions.stem: Who was Nigeria's first President when it became a Republic in 1963?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe became Nigeria's first President when the Republican Constitution of 1963 replaced the Queen with a Nigerian head of state.

questions.stem: Who was Nigeria's first Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was Nigeria's first and only Prime Minister, serving from 1960 until he was killed in the military coup of January 15, 1966.

questions.stem: What ended the First Republic of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The First Republic ended abruptly when the military overthrew the civilian government in the coup of January 15, 1966, led by Major Kaduna Nzeogwu.

questions.stem: Which constitution first introduced the American-style Presidential system to Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution was the first to introduce the Presidential system in Nigeria, creating an executive President, a Senate, and a House of Representatives modelled on the United States system.

questions.stem: The Second Republic in Nigeria began on which date?
questions.explanation: The Second Republic began on October 1, 1979 when President Shehu Shagari was inaugurated under the new 1979 Constitution.

questions.stem: How did the Second Republic come to an end?

options.A: A constitutional amendment dissolved the government
options.C: A military coup by Buhari and Idiagbon on December 31, 1983
options.D: The Supreme Court nullified Shagari's election

questions.explanation: The Second Republic ended on December 31, 1983 when Major General Muhammadu Buhari and Brigadier Tunde Idiagbon overthrew President Shehu Shagari in a military coup.

questions.stem: The 1989 Constitution drafted under IBB's regime was never fully implemented. Why?

options.A: It was rejected in a national referendum
options.B: IBB annulled the June 12, 1993 election and cancelled the transition programme
options.C: The Supreme Court declared it unconstitutional
options.D: ECOWAS intervened to prevent its implementation

questions.explanation: The 1989 Constitution was designed for the proposed Third Republic transition. It was never implemented because IBB annulled the June 12, 1993 election and aborted the transition to civilian rule.

questions.stem: How many times has the 1999 Constitution been formally amended?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution has been amended four times: First Alteration (2010), Second Alteration (2010), Third Alteration (2011), and Fourth Alteration (2017).

questions.stem: What was the purpose of the Willinks Commission of 1957-58?

options.A: To recommend a new federal capital
options.B: To investigate minority fears and recommend whether new states should be created
options.D: To negotiate Nigeria's independence from Britain

questions.explanation: The Willinks Commission (1957-58) was set up to investigate the fears of minority groups in Nigeria and to recommend whether new states should be created before independence.

questions.stem: In correct chronological order, which list of Nigerian constitutions is accurate?
questions.explanation: The correct chronological order of Nigeria's early constitutions is Clifford (1922), Richards (1946), Macpherson (1951), and Lyttleton (1954).

questions.stem: When was June 12 officially declared Democracy Day by President Buhari?
questions.explanation: President Muhammadu Buhari declared June 12 as Nigeria's Democracy Day on June 6, 2018, honouring MKO Abiola with a posthumous Grand Commander of the Federal Republic (GCFR) award.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian constitution first introduced the elective principle?
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was the first to introduce the elective principle, allowing Nigerians to elect a limited number of representatives to the Legislative Council.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian constitution first introduced regionalism?
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 was the first to introduce regionalism, dividing Nigeria into Northern, Western, and Eastern regions.

questions.stem: Which constitution transformed Nigeria into a formal Federation?
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 was the landmark constitution that formally established Nigeria as a federation.

questions.stem: Under which constitution did Nigeria become an independent sovereign nation?
questions.explanation: The Independence Constitution of 1960 was the instrument under which Nigeria became an independent sovereign nation on October 1, 1960.

questions.stem: Which constitution was drafted with the most Nigerian participation?
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is regarded as the constitution drafted with the broadest Nigerian participation, involving consultations at village, district, and national levels.

questions.stem: How many successful military coups has Nigeria experienced in total?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has experienced six successful military coups: January 1966, July 1966, 1975, 1983, 1985, and 1993.

questions.stem: Who led Nigeria's first military coup on January 15, 1966?
questions.explanation: Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu led Nigeria's first military coup on January 15, 1966, killing prominent leaders including Prime Minister Tafawa Balewa.

questions.stem: Who became Nigeria's first military Head of State following the January 1966 coup?
questions.explanation: Major General Johnson Thomas Umunnakwe Aguiyi-Ironsi assumed power on January 16, 1966, becoming Nigeria's first military Head of State after the Nzeogwu coup.

questions.stem: What was the significance of Aguiyi-Ironsi's Decree No. 34 of 1966?

options.B: It abolished the federal structure and unified Nigeria into a unitary state
options.D: It declared a state of emergency in the North

questions.explanation: Decree No. 34 of 1966 (the Unification Decree) issued by Aguiyi-Ironsi abolished Nigeria's federal structure and unified the country into a unitary state, causing outrage in the Northern region.

questions.stem: What happened to Aguiyi-Ironsi on July 29, 1966?

options.A: He voluntarily handed over power to Gowon
options.B: He was overthrown and killed in the Northern-led counter-coup
options.C: He resigned due to ill health

questions.explanation: Aguiyi-Ironsi was abducted from Government House in Ibadan and killed during the Northern-led counter-coup of July 29, 1966, along with his host, Governor Adekunle Fajuyi.

questions.stem: Who led the July 29, 1966 counter-coup that killed Aguiyi-Ironsi?

options.B: Lieutenant Colonel Murtala Muhammed and Theophilus Yakubu Danjuma

questions.explanation: The July 1966 counter-coup was led by Northern military officers including Lieutenant Colonel Murtala Muhammed and Theophilus Yakubu Danjuma.

questions.stem: Who succeeded Aguiyi-Ironsi as Head of State after the July 1966 counter-coup?
questions.explanation: Lieutenant Colonel (later General) Yakubu Gowon came to power on August 1, 1966 after the counter-coup that killed Aguiyi-Ironsi.

questions.stem: What major armed conflict occurred during Gowon's regime?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War, also known as the Biafran War, was the defining event of Gowon's regime, fought between federal forces and the secessionist Republic of Biafra from 1967 to 1970.

questions.stem: Gowon was famous for which statement at the end of the Civil War in 1970?
questions.explanation: At the end of the Civil War on January 15, 1970, General Gowon declared 'No victor, no vanquished' as a message of national reconciliation and unity.

questions.stem: How was General Yakubu Gowon removed from power in 1975?

options.A: He lost a general election to Shehu Shagari
options.B: He was assassinated by Lt. Colonel Dimka
options.C: He was overthrown in a bloodless coup by Brigadier Murtala Muhammed while abroad
options.D: He voluntarily resigned and handed over to Obasanjo

questions.explanation: Gowon was overthrown in a bloodless coup on July 29, 1975 while he was attending an OAU summit in Kampala, Uganda. Brigadier Murtala Muhammed led the coup.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an achievement of Gowon's regime?

options.D: Introduction of the Structural Adjustment Programme

questions.explanation: The Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) was introduced by General Ibrahim Babangida, not Gowon. Gowon's achievements include creating 12 states, winning the Civil War, and co-founding ECOWAS.

questions.stem: For what is General Murtala Muhammed's brief regime (1975-1976) best remembered?

options.A: Winning the Civil War and reconciliation
options.B: Moving the capital to Abuja, creating more states, and purging the civil service

questions.explanation: Murtala Muhammed's regime is remembered for designating Abuja as the new federal capital (1976), creating 7 more states (bringing the total to 19), and decisively purging corrupt officials from the civil service.

questions.stem: Who assassinated General Murtala Muhammed and when?

options.A: Lt. Colonel Buka Suka Dimka on February 13, 1976

questions.explanation: General Murtala Muhammed was assassinated on February 13, 1976 during an abortive coup attempt led by Lt. Colonel Buka Suka Dimka.

questions.stem: What happened to Lt. Colonel Dimka after the failed February 1976 coup?

options.A: He fled into exile in Ghana
options.B: He was arrested, tried, and executed by firing squad on May 15, 1976
options.C: He was pardoned and released after a year
options.D: He died in prison from illness

questions.explanation: Lt. Colonel Buka Suka Dimka was captured after his failed coup attempt, tried by a military tribunal, and executed by firing squad on May 15, 1976.

questions.stem: For what historic democratic action is Obasanjo's first military regime (1976-1979) known?

options.B: Being the first military ruler to willingly hand over power to an elected civilian government

questions.explanation: General Olusegun Obasanjo is celebrated as the first Nigerian military ruler to voluntarily hand over power to a democratically elected civilian government, handing over to President Shehu Shagari in 1979.

questions.stem: Who led the coup that ended the Second Republic on December 31, 1983?

options.A: General Ibrahim Babangida and General Aliyu
options.B: Major General Muhammadu Buhari and Brigadier Tunde Idiagbon
options.C: General Sani Abacha and Ernest Shonekan

questions.explanation: The Second Republic ended on December 31, 1983 when Major General Muhammadu Buhari and Brigadier Tunde Idiagbon overthrew President Shehu Shagari's government.

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT associated with the Buhari/Idiagbon regime of 1984-1985?
questions.explanation: The Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) was introduced by General Ibrahim Babangida, not Buhari. The Buhari regime is known for WAI, Decree 2, and Decree 4.

questions.stem: Who overthrew General Muhammadu Buhari and when?
questions.explanation: General Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida (IBB) ousted General Buhari in a palace coup on August 27, 1985.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a major achievement/event associated with IBB's regime (1985-1993)?

options.A: Introduction of the War Against Indiscipline
options.C: The June 12, 1993 presidential election and its annulment

questions.explanation: IBB's regime is most controversially defined by the June 12, 1993 presidential election - widely regarded as Nigeria's freest election - which IBB annulled on June 23, 1993.

questions.stem: What economic programme did IBB introduce that significantly restructured Nigeria's economy?

options.C: National Economic Empowerment and Development Strategy (NEEDS)

questions.explanation: General Ibrahim Babangida introduced the Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP), which involved deregulation, devaluation of the naira, and removal of subsidies as conditions of IMF/World Bank policy.

questions.stem: Who headed the Interim National Government (ING) after IBB stepped down in 1993?
questions.explanation: Ernest Shonekan headed the Interim National Government from August 27, 1993, after IBB stepped down, before being overthrown by General Sani Abacha on November 17, 1993.

questions.stem: When did General Sani Abacha seize power from Ernest Shonekan?
questions.explanation: General Sani Abacha overthrew Ernest Shonekan's Interim National Government on November 17, 1993 to become military Head of State.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Sani Abacha's regime (1993-1998)?

options.B: Extreme repression, looting, and international isolation
options.D: Free press and human rights reforms

questions.explanation: Abacha's regime is characterised by extreme political repression, the execution of activists like Ken Saro-Wiwa, imprisonment of MKO Abiola, massive looting of the treasury, and Nigeria's international isolation.

questions.stem: Which senior officer was executed for alleged involvement in the Dimka coup of 1976?
questions.explanation: General Iliya Bisalla was the senior officer executed by firing squad for alleged involvement in the Dimka coup of February 13, 1976 that killed Murtala Muhammed.

questions.stem: How did General Sani Abacha leave power?

options.A: He was overthrown in a military coup
options.B: He was assassinated by Lt. Colonel Dimka
options.C: He died suddenly on June 8, 1998 under mysterious circumstances
options.D: He voluntarily stepped aside under international pressure

questions.explanation: General Sani Abacha died on June 8, 1998, officially from a heart attack, though many believe he was poisoned. He died while still in power.

questions.stem: Who succeeded Abacha and organised the transition to the Fourth Republic?
questions.explanation: General Abdulsalami Abubakar became Head of State on June 9, 1998 after Abacha's death, and organised the elections that produced President Obasanjo and the Fourth Republic in 1999.

questions.stem: Who was the first Nigerian Head of State to be killed while in office?
questions.explanation: Major General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi was the first Head of State killed while in office, assassinated during the counter-coup of July 29, 1966.

questions.stem: Where was Aguiyi-Ironsi killed and who died alongside him?

options.A: Dodan Barracks, Lagos - alongside General Gowon
options.B: Government House, Ibadan - alongside Governor Adekunle Fajuyi
options.C: Government House, Kaduna - alongside the Sardauna
options.D: State House, Enugu - alongside Colonel Ojukwu

questions.explanation: Aguiyi-Ironsi was abducted from Government House in Ibadan and killed alongside his host, Governor Adekunle Fajuyi of the Western Region, during the July 1966 counter-coup.

questions.stem: Who was assassinated in the January 15, 1966 coup alongside Prime Minister Tafawa Balewa?

options.A: Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, and Chike Obi
options.B: Ahmadu Bello, Samuel Akintola, and Festus Okotie-Eboh
options.C: Yakubu Gowon, Murtala Muhammed, and Philip Effiong
options.D: Ernest Shonekan, Shehu Shagari, and Goodluck Jonathan

questions.explanation: The January 15, 1966 coup claimed the lives of Prime Minister Tafawa Balewa, the Sardauna Ahmadu Bello (Premier of Northern Region), Chief Samuel Akintola (Premier of Western Region), and Finance Minister Chief Festus Okotie-Eboh.

questions.stem: Who killed the Sardauna of Sokoto, Sir Ahmadu Bello, on January 15, 1966?

options.A: Major Nzeogwu personally led the attack on his home in Kaduna
options.B: Lt. Colonel Murtala Muhammed in Lagos

questions.explanation: Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu personally led the attack on the Sardauna's home in Kaduna on January 15, 1966, killing Sir Ahmadu Bello.

questions.stem: What was the fate of Ken Saro-Wiwa and when did it occur?

options.A: He was imprisoned for life in 1993
options.B: He was killed by a parcel bomb on October 19, 1986
options.C: He was executed by hanging on November 10, 1995
options.D: He died in detention on July 7, 1998

questions.explanation: Ken Saro-Wiwa, the writer and Ogoni environmental activist, was executed by hanging on November 10, 1995, along with eight other Ogoni activists (the Ogoni Nine) under Abacha's orders.

questions.stem: Who were the 'Ogoni Nine'?

options.A: Nine Biafran generals who surrendered in 1970
options.B: Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists executed by Abacha's government in 1995
options.C: Nine NCNC founding members arrested in 1944
options.D: Nine Aba Women's Riot leaders executed in 1929

questions.explanation: The 'Ogoni Nine' refers to Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight fellow activists (including Saturday Dobee, Nordu Eawo, Daniel Gbooko, Paul Levula, Felix Nuate, Baribor Bera, Barinem Kiobel, and John Kpuinen) executed on November 10, 1995.

questions.stem: What was the international consequence of Ken Saro-Wiwa's execution?

options.A: Nigeria was admitted to the United Nations
options.B: Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth of Nations
options.D: ECOWAS imposed trade sanctions on Nigeria

questions.explanation: The execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa triggered Nigeria's suspension from the Commonwealth of Nations, along with widespread international condemnation and recalls of ambassadors.

questions.stem: What happened to Chief MKO Abiola and when did he die?

options.A: He was executed by Abacha on November 10, 1995
options.B: He was assassinated by gunmen on June 4, 1996
options.C: He died in detention on July 7, 1998
options.D: He died in a car accident in 2001

questions.explanation: MKO Abiola, widely believed to have won the June 12, 1993 election, was arrested in 1994 and died in detention on July 7, 1998 - the day he was scheduled to meet US officials. The official cause was heart failure, but many suspect poisoning.

questions.stem: Who was Kudirat Abiola and what happened to her?

options.A: MKO Abiola's daughter; she died in prison in 1997
options.B: MKO Abiola's wife and democracy activist; she was assassinated on June 4, 1996
options.C: A female senator killed in the 1966 coup
options.D: An Ogoni activist executed with Ken Saro-Wiwa

questions.explanation: Kudirat Abiola was the wife of MKO Abiola and a prominent pro-democracy activist. She was shot by gunmen while driving in Lagos on June 4, 1996. Major Hamza AlMustapha, Abacha's Chief Security Officer, was later convicted for her killing.

questions.stem: Who was Dele Giwa and how did he die?

options.A: A military general killed in the 1966 coup
options.B: The founding editor of Newswatch magazine, killed by a parcel bomb on October 19, 1986
options.D: A civil war commander killed at the Battle of Nsukka

questions.explanation: Dele Giwa was the founding editor of Newswatch magazine. He was killed by a parcel bomb delivered to his home on October 19, 1986. The murder has never been officially solved, though many suspect the Babangida government.

questions.stem: How did President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua leave office?

options.A: He was defeated in the 2011 election
options.B: He was overthrown in a military coup
options.C: He resigned due to the June 12 crisis
options.D: He died in office on May 5, 2010 from a prolonged illness

questions.explanation: President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua died in office on May 5, 2010 after a prolonged battle with pericarditis and kidney complications, making Vice President Goodluck Jonathan the new President.

questions.stem: Who assassinated Attorney General Bola Ige and when?

options.A: Unknown gunmen on December 23, 2001 at his Ibadan residence

questions.explanation: Chief Bola Ige, Nigeria's Attorney General and Minister of Justice under Obasanjo, was assassinated on December 23, 2001 at his residence in Ibadan. His killers were never officially prosecuted.

questions.stem: When was Lagos formally annexed as a British colony?
questions.explanation: Lagos was formally annexed as the Colony of Lagos on August 6, 1861, marking the beginning of direct British colonial rule in what would become Nigeria.

questions.stem: When was the Royal Niger Company chartered?
questions.explanation: The Royal Niger Company was chartered in 1886 when the National African Company, led by Sir George Taubman Goldie, received a royal charter from the British government.

questions.stem: When were both the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria and the Protectorate of Southern Nigeria established?
questions.explanation: Both the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria and the Protectorate of Southern Nigeria were established on January 1, 1900, when the British government took over from the Royal Niger Company.

questions.stem: On what date did the amalgamation of Nigeria take place?
questions.explanation: The amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria by Lord Lugard took place on January 1, 1914, creating the single entity known as Nigeria.

questions.stem: When was Nigeria's Labour Strike led by Michael Imodu?
questions.explanation: The general Labour Strike led by Michael Imodu occurred in June 1945, paralyzing Nigeria for 37 days and pressuring the British into constitutional changes that resulted in the Richards Constitution of 1946.

questions.stem: In what year did the Western and Eastern Regions of Nigeria gain self-governance?
questions.explanation: The Western and Eastern Regions of Nigeria gained self-governance in 1957; the Northern Region followed in 1959, ahead of full national independence in 1960.

questions.stem: On what date did Nigeria gain independence?
questions.explanation: Nigeria gained independence from British rule on October 1, 1960, which is now celebrated annually as Independence Day.

questions.stem: On what date was the Republic of Biafra declared?
questions.explanation: Colonel Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu declared the Republic of Biafra on May 30, 1967, triggering the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: On what date did the Nigerian Civil War officially end?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War ended on January 15, 1970 when Biafran forces surrendered. General Philip Effiong signed the instrument of surrender after Ojukwu had fled to Ivory Coast.

questions.stem: When was ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) formed?
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was founded on May 28, 1975, with Nigeria under General Gowon as a founding and leading member.

questions.stem: When were the controversial June 12 presidential elections held, and when were the results annulled?
questions.explanation: The presidential election was held on June 12, 1993, and IBB annulled the results just eleven days later on June 23, 1993, sparking a massive political crisis.

questions.stem: When did Abacha die?
questions.explanation: General Sani Abacha died on June 8, 1998, officially from a heart attack. His death paved the way for Nigeria's return to democracy in 1999.

questions.stem: On what date was President Olusegun Obasanjo inaugurated to begin the Fourth Republic?
questions.explanation: President Olusegun Obasanjo was inaugurated on May 29, 1999, marking the beginning of the Fourth Republic and Nigeria's current democratic era.

questions.stem: When was the NNPC (Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation) established?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) was established in 1977 under General Olusegun Obasanjo's military regime to manage Nigeria's oil and gas resources.

questions.stem: When was the Aba Women's Riot?
questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riot (Ogu Umunwanyi - Women's War) occurred in 1929 as a spontaneous uprising of Igbo and Ibibio women against British taxation and the exploitative warrant chief system.

questions.stem: When was President Buhari's landmark election victory over a sitting president recorded?
questions.explanation: On March 28, 2015, Muhammadu Buhari of the APC defeated incumbent President Goodluck Jonathan of the PDP - the first time a sitting Nigerian president was defeated at the polls.

questions.stem: When was President Bola Ahmed Tinubu inaugurated?
questions.explanation: Bola Ahmed Tinubu was inaugurated as Nigeria's President on May 29, 2023, succeeding President Muhammadu Buhari.

questions.stem: What was the first political party in Nigeria and who founded it?

options.A: NCNC, founded by Nnamdi Azikiwe in 1944
options.B: Action Group, founded by Obafemi Awolowo in 1951
options.C: NNDP, founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923
options.D: NPC, founded by Ahmadu Bello in 1951

questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923 was the first formal political party in Nigeria.

questions.stem: When was the NCNC founded and by whom?
questions.explanation: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), later renamed the National Council of Nigerian Citizens, was founded in 1944 by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe.

questions.stem: The Action Group (AG) was founded in 1951 by which nationalist leader?
questions.explanation: Chief Obafemi Awolowo founded the Action Group in 1951, growing it out of the Egbe Omo Oduduwa cultural organisation, as the main Yoruba nationalist political party.

questions.stem: The Northern People's Congress (NPC) was founded in 1951 by whom?

options.B: Sardauna Ahmadu Bello with Tafawa Balewa

questions.explanation: The Northern People's Congress (NPC) was founded in 1951 by the Sardauna of Sokoto, Sir Ahmadu Bello, with the support of Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa.

questions.stem: What two parties did IBB create for the proposed Third Republic transition?

options.C: Social Democratic Party (SDP) and National Republican Convention (NRC)

questions.explanation: IBB created and funded exactly two parties for his managed transition - the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the National Republican Convention (NRC) - to prevent fragmentation.

questions.stem: Who was MKO Abiola's running mate in the June 12, 1993 presidential election?
questions.explanation: Ambassador Babagana Kingibe was MKO Abiola's running mate in the June 12, 1993 presidential election on the SDP ticket.

questions.stem: Which party did Olusegun Obasanjo use to win the 1999 presidential election?
questions.explanation: Olusegun Obasanjo won the 1999 presidential election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), defeating Chief Olu Falae of the AD/APP.

questions.stem: What made the 2015 presidential election historically significant?

options.A: It was Nigeria's first multiparty election
options.B: It was the first time an incumbent president was defeated at the polls
options.C: It was conducted entirely by electronic voting
options.D: It was the first election supervised by INEC

questions.explanation: The 2015 election was the first time a sitting Nigerian president (Goodluck Jonathan) was defeated at the polls by an opposition candidate (Muhammadu Buhari of the APC), resulting in a historic peaceful transfer of power.

questions.stem: The APC that won the 2015 election was a merger of which parties?

options.B: ACN, CPC, ANPP, and nPDP factions
