questions.explanation: The All Progressives Congress (APC) was formed from a merger of the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), Congress for Progressive Change (CPC), All Nigeria Peoples Party (ANPP), and factions of the new PDP (nPDP).

questions.stem: Who were the three main candidates in the 2023 Nigerian presidential election?

options.B: Tinubu (APC), Atiku Abubakar (PDP), and Peter Obi (Labour Party)

questions.explanation: The 2023 presidential election was a notable three-way contest between Bola Tinubu (APC), Atiku Abubakar (PDP), and Peter Obi (Labour Party), with Tinubu winning.

questions.stem: What was the immediate trigger of the Nigerian Civil War?

options.A: The annulment of the June 12 election
options.B: The massacres of Igbo people in the North following the July 1966 counter-coup

questions.explanation: The killings of thousands of Igbo people in Northern Nigeria after the July 1966 counter-coup triggered a mass exodus of Igbos back to the Eastern Region, setting the stage for Biafra's declaration.

questions.stem: Who was the leader of Biafra during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: Colonel Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu, then Military Governor of the Eastern Region, declared the Republic of Biafra and led it throughout the Civil War.

questions.stem: What was the Aburi Accord?

options.A: The document Biafra used to declare independence
options.B: A peace agreement signed in Ghana proposing a loose confederation for Nigeria
options.D: The agreement that ended the Civil War in 1970

questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord was a peace agreement signed in Aburi, Ghana in January 1967 between Gowon and Ojukwu, proposing a loose confederation. It was later repudiated by the Gowon government, contributing to the war.

questions.stem: Why did Gowon create 12 states in May 1967, just before the Civil War began?

options.A: To prepare for a new constitution
options.B: To break regional power and undercut Biafra's support by giving minorities their own states
options.D: To satisfy the demands of the Aburi Accord

questions.explanation: By creating 12 states, Gowon weakened the three regions' power and specifically undercut Biafra's claim by carving out separate states for minorities within the Eastern Region who did not support secession.

questions.stem: Who signed the Biafran instrument of surrender on January 15, 1970?
questions.explanation: General Philip Effiong signed the instrument of surrender on behalf of Biafra on January 15, 1970. Ojukwu had fled to Ivory Coast four days earlier on January 11, 1970.

questions.stem: What was the name of Gowon's post-war policy for rebuilding Nigeria?
questions.explanation: After the Civil War, Gowon launched the 3Rs policy - Reconciliation, Rehabilitation, and Reconstruction - to heal the nation and reintegrate former Biafrans into Nigerian society.

questions.stem: Which federal commander was nicknamed 'Black Scorpion' during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: General Benjamin Adekunle earned the nickname 'Black Scorpion' for his fierce and aggressive command of the 3rd Marine Commando Division during the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: Who was Nigeria's President from 1999 to 2007?
questions.explanation: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo of the PDP served as Nigeria's President from 1999 to 2007, completing two terms as the first President of the Fourth Republic.

questions.stem: How did Goodluck Jonathan become President of Nigeria?

options.B: He was appointed by the military
options.C: He became President after Yar'Adua's death in office on May 5, 2010
options.D: He defeated Obasanjo in the 2007 primary

questions.explanation: Goodluck Jonathan was Vice President under Yar'Adua and became acting President in February 2010 when Yar'Adua fell critically ill, then was fully sworn in as President on May 6, 2010 after Yar'Adua's death.

questions.stem: What was the #EndSARS protest and when did it occur?

options.A: A protest against fuel subsidy removal in May 2023
options.B: A youth protest in October 2020 demanding the disbandment of the Special Anti-Robbery Squad
options.C: A student strike against poor university funding in 2019
options.D: A protest against the 2015 election results

questions.explanation: #EndSARS was a nationwide youth protest in October 2020 demanding the immediate disbandment of SARS (Special Anti-Robbery Squad), a police unit notorious for brutality and extrajudicial killings.

questions.stem: What happened at the Lekki Toll Gate on October 20, 2020?

options.A: Protesters destroyed the toll gate infrastructure
options.B: Nigerian Army and police opened fire on peaceful #EndSARS protesters
options.C: SARS officers were arrested by protesters
options.D: President Buhari addressed protesters at the toll gate

questions.explanation: On October 20, 2020 (now known as 'Bloody Tuesday'), Nigerian soldiers and police opened fire on peaceful #EndSARS protesters at the Lekki Toll Gate in Lagos, causing international outrage. The exact death toll remains disputed.

questions.stem: What major economic policy did President Tinubu announce on his inauguration day, May 29, 2023?

options.A: The introduction of a new naira note
options.B: The removal of the fuel subsidy
options.C: The creation of a new national development plan

questions.explanation: On his inauguration day, President Tinubu announced the removal of Nigeria's long-standing fuel subsidy with the phrase 'subsidy is gone,' immediately causing fuel price increases nationwide.

questions.stem: What was the naira redesign policy and under whose administration was it implemented?

options.B: Buhari's CBN Governor Godwin Emefiele redesigned the N200, N500, and N1000 notes in 2022-2023
options.C: Obasanjo redesigned the naira in 2005 to combat counterfeiting
options.D: Jonathan redesigned the naira in 2012 to mark Nigeria's centenary

questions.explanation: Under Buhari's directive, CBN Governor Godwin Emefiele redesigned the N200, N500, and N1000 notes in 2022-2023, causing a severe cash crunch that disrupted millions of Nigerians during a critical election period.

questions.stem: Where did Boko Haram originate and who founded it?

options.A: Kano State, founded by Abubakar Shekau around 2009
options.B: Maiduguri, Borno State, founded by Mohammed Yusuf around 2002
options.C: Sokoto State, founded by Mohammed Yusuf in 1995
options.D: Zamfara State, founded by Abubakar Shekau in 2002

questions.explanation: Boko Haram emerged in Maiduguri, Borno State around 2002 under the leadership of Mohammed Yusuf. It launched a full insurgency in 2009 after Yusuf was killed by Nigerian police.

questions.stem: What was the Chibok Girls kidnapping and when did it occur?

options.A: Boko Haram abducted 276 schoolgirls from Chibok, Borno State on April 14-15, 2014
options.B: ISWAP kidnapped 300 schoolgirls from Dapchi, Yobe State in 2018
options.C: Fulani herdsmen abducted 200 girls from Zamfara State in 2020
options.D: Boko Haram kidnapped 276 boys from Kagara, Niger State in 2021

questions.explanation: On April 14-15, 2014, Boko Haram abducted 276 schoolgirls from the Government Girls Secondary School in Chibok, Borno State, sparking the global #BringBackOurGirls campaign.

questions.stem: When was the EFCC established and who was its first chairman?
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was established in 2003 under President Obasanjo to combat financial crime. Malam Nuhu Ribadu served as its first Executive Chairman from 2003 to 2007.

questions.stem: What is ICPC and when was it established?

options.A: Independent Corrupt Practices Commission, established in 2003
options.B: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, established in 2000
options.C: International Committee on Political Corruption, established in 1999
options.D: Institutional Corruption Prevention Committee, established in 2007

questions.explanation: The ICPC (Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission) was established in 2000 under President Obasanjo, focused specifically on institutional and public sector corruption.

questions.stem: What was the Niger Delta Amnesty Programme and when was it launched?

options.A: A programme to resettle oil spill victims, launched in 2003 by Obasanjo
options.B: A programme launched by Yar'Adua in 2009 offering militants amnesty in exchange for surrendering weapons
options.C: An NDDC initiative to build infrastructure in the Niger Delta, launched in 2001
options.D: A Buhari-era programme to prosecute oil pipeline vandals, launched in 2016

questions.explanation: The Niger Delta Amnesty Programme was launched in 2009 by President Yar'Adua, offering amnesty to militants who surrendered weapons in exchange for training and monthly stipends, significantly reducing oil pipeline attacks.

questions.stem: Who leads IPOB (Indigenous People of Biafra)?
questions.explanation: IPOB, the separatist group advocating for an independent Biafra state, is led by Nnamdi Kanu, who was re-arrested in June 2021 after being renditioned from Kenya to Nigeria.

questions.stem: What was the significance of the Electoral Act 2022 signed by President Buhari?

options.A: It created INEC and established Nigeria's electoral commission
options.B: It introduced biometric voter verification (BVAS) and electronic result transmission
options.C: It reduced the voting age from 18 to 16
options.D: It banned military officers from contesting elections

questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2022 significantly reformed Nigeria's electoral process by introducing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for biometric verification and mandating electronic transmission of results.

questions.stem: Who is widely regarded as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism'?
questions.explanation: Herbert Samuel Heelas Macaulay (1864-1945) is regarded as the father of Nigerian nationalism. He founded the NNDP in 1923 and devoted his life to anti-colonial activism.

questions.stem: Who was known as 'Zik of Africa'?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe earned the title 'Zik of Africa' for his pan-African vision. He was Nigeria's first President, founder of the NCNC, and owner of the West African Pilot newspaper.

questions.stem: What was Chief Obafemi Awolowo's most celebrated achievement as Premier of Western Region?

options.B: Introduction of free primary education and free healthcare in the West

questions.explanation: Chief Obafemi Awolowo is most celebrated for introducing free primary education and free healthcare in the Western Region during his tenure as Premier from 1954 to 1959, setting a model for social welfare policy in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Who was the Sardauna of Sokoto?
questions.explanation: Sir Ahmadu Bello (1909-1966) held the traditional title Sardauna of Sokoto. He was Premier of Northern Region, founder of the NPC, and the most dominant political figure in pre-independence Nigeria.

questions.stem: What was Abubakar Tafawa Balewa's popular title and what is he remembered for?

options.A: 'Zik of Africa' - first President of Nigeria
options.B: 'Golden Voice of Africa' - first and only Prime Minister of Nigeria

questions.explanation: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was nicknamed the 'Golden Voice of Africa' for his exceptional oratory. He served as Nigeria's first and only Prime Minister from 1960 until his assassination on January 15, 1966.

questions.stem: Who was Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti and what is she known for?

options.A: A military officer who led the counter-coup in 1966
options.B: An activist and women's rights pioneer known as the 'Lioness of Lisabi', and mother of Fela Kuti
options.C: Nigeria's first female senator, elected in 1979
options.D: A nationalist who founded the NCNC alongside Azikiwe

questions.explanation: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti (1900-1978) was a prominent educator, women's rights advocate, and anti-colonial activist known as the 'Lioness of Lisabi.' She led the Abeokuta Women's Union and was the mother of Afrobeat legend Fela Kuti.

questions.stem: What was the Aba Women's Riot (Ogu Umunwanyi) of 1929 about?

options.A: Resistance to British plans to impose taxes on women and the exploitative warrant chief system
options.B: A protest against the exclusion of women from the 1922 Clifford Constitution elections
options.C: A workers' strike by female factory workers in Aba
options.D: A protest against the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria

questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riot of 1929 was a spontaneous uprising of Igbo and Ibibio women against proposed British taxation of women and the corrupt warrant chief system. It is one of the first major anti-colonial uprisings in West Africa.

questions.stem: What was the human cost of the Aba Women's Riot (1929)?

options.A: 5-10 women were killed by British forces in Aba
options.B: 32-50 women were killed by British forces in Aba and Calabar
options.C: Over 100 women were imprisoned without trial
options.D: No deaths occurred; the protest was resolved peacefully

questions.explanation: British colonial forces killed between 32 and 50 women in Aba and Calabar during the 1929 Women's Riot, an act that drew sharp criticism and intensified anti-colonial sentiment.

questions.stem: Who introduced the policy of Indirect Rule in Nigeria and what was it?

options.A: Sir Hugh Clifford - governing through direct British administrators
options.B: Lord Frederick Lugard - governing through existing traditional rulers
options.C: Sir Arthur Richards - governing through elected councils
options.D: Sir John Macpherson - governing through regional assemblies

questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard introduced the system of Indirect Rule in Nigeria, which involved governing the colonised population through their own existing traditional rulers and institutions under British supervision, pioneered first in Northern Nigeria.

questions.stem: What was the significance of the 1945 General Strike in Nigerian history?

options.A: It led directly to Nigerian independence in 1945
options.B: Led by Michael Imodu, it paralysed Nigeria for 37 days and forced the British to make constitutional changes
options.C: It was the first workers' strike in West Africa
options.D: It led to the formation of the NCNC

questions.explanation: The June 1945 General Strike, led by labour leader Michael Imodu, shut down Nigeria for 37 days. The resulting pressure on the British contributed to constitutional revisions that produced the Richards Constitution of 1946.

questions.stem: What was the NNDP and what significance did it have in Nigeria's political history?

options.A: Northern Nigeria Democratic Party - the ruling party of Northern Region
options.B: Nigerian National Democratic Party - the first political party in Nigeria, founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923
options.C: National Nigeria Development Plan - an economic blueprint by Gowon
options.D: Nigerian National Defence Programme - a military development strategy

questions.explanation: The NNDP (Nigerian National Democratic Party) founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923 was the first political party in Nigeria, formed to contest the limited elections introduced by the Clifford Constitution.

questions.stem: What is the significance of June 12 in Nigerian history?

options.A: The date Nigeria gained independence in 1960
options.B: The date of the 1966 coup that ended the First Republic
options.C: The date of the 1993 presidential election widely believed to have been won by MKO Abiola
options.D: The date President Tinubu was inaugurated in 2023

questions.explanation: June 12, 1993 is regarded as Nigeria's most symbolic democracy date - the day of the freest and fairest presidential election, widely believed to have been won by MKO Abiola but annulled by IBB eleven days later. It is now officially Democracy Day.

questions.stem: How many states did Nigeria have when it gained independence in 1960?
questions.explanation: At independence in 1960, Nigeria was divided into three regions - Northern, Eastern, and Western - not states. The first state creation (12 states) was by Gowon in 1967.

questions.stem: What is the significance of Shehu Shagari's 1979-1983 presidency?

options.A: He was the first military President of Nigeria
options.B: He was the first elected executive President of Nigeria under the new presidential system
options.C: He introduced the Structural Adjustment Programme
options.D: He created the 36-state structure still in use today

questions.explanation: Shehu Shagari of the NPN became Nigeria's first elected executive President under the American-style presidential system introduced by the 1979 Constitution, beginning the Second Republic.

questions.stem: What is the Third Tier of government in Nigeria and how many units does it consist of?
questions.explanation: The third tier of government in Nigeria is the Local Government Area (LGA), and there are 774 LGAs in total spread across the 36 states and FCT.

questions.stem: What does the acronym ECOWAS stand for and who was Nigeria's key role in its founding?

options.A: Economic Cooperation of West African States - Nigeria was the host country
options.B: Economic Community of West African States - Nigeria under Gowon was a founding and driving member
options.C: Eastern Community of West African Settlements - Nigeria joined as a charter member
options.D: Economic Council of West Africa and Sahel - Nigeria led post-civil war reconstruction

questions.explanation: ECOWAS stands for the Economic Community of West African States, founded on May 28, 1975. Nigeria under General Gowon was a key founding member and has historically been the dominant power within the organisation.

questions.stem: What was the 'War Against Indiscipline' (WAI) introduced by the Buhari regime?

options.A: A military campaign against Boko Haram in the North-East
options.B: A nationwide campaign to enforce orderliness, punctuality, and discipline among citizens
options.C: An anti-corruption drive targeting military officers
options.D: A programme to disarm Niger Delta militants

questions.explanation: The War Against Indiscipline (WAI) was a nationwide social re-orientation campaign launched by the Buhari/Idiagbon regime to instil discipline among Nigerians - enforcing queue culture, environmental cleanliness, and punctuality.

questions.stem: What was Decree 2 of 1984, introduced under Buhari's regime?

options.B: A decree allowing detention of persons without trial for up to three months

questions.explanation: Decree 2 of 1984 under the Buhari regime allowed the government to detain any person considered a security risk without trial for up to three months, a provision widely condemned as a tool for suppressing dissent.

questions.stem: What was Decree 4 of 1984, introduced under Buhari's regime?

options.A: A decree allowing detention without trial
options.B: A decree that muzzled the press by criminalising embarrassing publications about the government

questions.explanation: Decree 4 of 1984 made it a criminal offence to publish anything deemed embarrassing or harmful to the military government, effectively muzzling the press. It was used to prosecute journalists.

questions.stem: What were the three geopolitical regions into which Nigeria was divided by the Richards Constitution of 1946?
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 divided Nigeria into three administrative regions: the Northern, Eastern, and Western regions, establishing the basis for Nigeria's federal structure.

questions.stem: How long is a presidential tenure in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Under the 1999 Constitution, a Nigerian President serves a term of four years and is eligible for re-election for a maximum of two terms.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian military ruler created the 19-state structure?

options.B: Murtala Muhammed - raised the total to 19 by creating 7 additional states in 1976

questions.explanation: General Murtala Muhammed raised Nigeria's state count to 19 by creating 7 additional states in 1976, building on the 12 states created by Gowon in 1967.

questions.stem: Which military ruler increased Nigeria's states to 30, and later to 36?

options.A: Gowon increased to 30; Obasanjo increased to 36
options.B: IBB increased from 19 to 21 and then to 30; Abacha increased to 36
options.C: Murtala increased to 30; IBB increased to 36
options.D: Buhari increased to 30; Abdulsalami increased to 36

questions.explanation: Ibrahim Babangida progressively increased Nigeria's states from 19 to 21 (1987) and then to 30 (1991). General Sani Abacha later created 6 more states in 1996, bringing the total to 36, which is the current number.

questions.stem: What was the role of the Royal Niger Company in Nigeria's colonial history?

options.A: It drafted the first constitution for Nigeria
options.B: It administered the Niger territories on behalf of the British government from 1886 until 1900
options.C: It built the first railway from Lagos to Kano
options.D: It served as Nigeria's central bank before independence

questions.explanation: The Royal Niger Company, led by Sir George Taubman Goldie and chartered in 1886, administered the Niger territories commercially and politically on behalf of Britain until the British government revoked its charter and took direct control on January 1, 1900.

questions.stem: What does the acronym SARS stand for in the context of the 2020 Nigerian protests?
questions.explanation: SARS stands for Special Anti-Robbery Squad. It was a unit of the Nigeria Police Force established in 1992 to combat armed robbery but became notorious for extrajudicial killings, torture, and extortion, leading to the #EndSARS protests of October 2020.

questions.stem: What was Ernest Shonekan's formal title as head of Nigeria's transitional government in 1993?

options.B: President of the Interim National Government (ING)
options.C: Chairman of the Provisional Ruling Council

questions.explanation: Ernest Shonekan led the Interim National Government (ING) as its head from August 27, 1993, when IBB stepped down, until he was overthrown by General Sani Abacha on November 17, 1993.

questions.stem: What is Nigeria's national motto?

options.C: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress

questions.explanation: Nigeria's national motto is 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress,' reflecting the aspirations of the country's diverse peoples.

questions.stem: What was the name of the political alliance formed between the NPC and NNDP for the 1964 Federal Election?
questions.explanation: For the 1964 Federal Elections, the NPC and NNDP formed the Nigerian National Alliance (NNA), which faced the United Progressive Grand Alliance (UPGA) - a coalition of the NCNC and Action Group.

questions.stem: When did Goodluck Jonathan first act as President before being fully sworn in?
questions.explanation: Goodluck Jonathan assumed acting Presidential powers on February 9, 2010 when the National Assembly passed a resolution citing the doctrine of necessity, as Yar'Adua was incapacitated abroad. He was fully sworn in after Yar'Adua's death on May 6, 2010.

questions.stem: What was the Aburi Accord and why did it fail?

options.A: A peace deal signed in Aburi, Ghana in 1967 proposing a confederation; it failed because Gowon later repudiated it
options.B: A ceasefire agreement signed in 1970 to end the Civil War
options.C: A constitutional agreement that created the 12-state structure
options.D: An ECOWAS peacekeeping agreement brokered in 1975

questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord was signed in January 1967 between Gowon and Ojukwu in Aburi, Ghana, proposing a loose confederation as a compromise to prevent war. It collapsed when Gowon's government - under pressure from civil servants and officials - repudiated key terms upon return to Lagos.

questions.stem: When was Goodluck Jonathan fully sworn in as President of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Goodluck Jonathan was fully sworn in as President on May 6, 2010, the day after President Yar'Adua's death on May 5, 2010.

questions.stem: What was IBB's full name?
questions.explanation: IBB's full name is Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida. He ruled Nigeria as military Head of State from August 27, 1985 to August 27, 1993.

questions.stem: Who was the CBN Governor suspended by President Tinubu in June 2023?
questions.explanation: Godwin Emefiele, who had controversially implemented the naira redesign policy, was suspended and later arrested by President Tinubu in June 2023. Yemi Cardoso was subsequently appointed as the new CBN Governor.

questions.stem: What is the composition of Nigeria's National Assembly?

options.A: Senate with 109 members and House of Representatives with 360 members
options.B: Senate with 120 members and House of Representatives with 300 members
options.C: Senate with 109 members and House of Representatives with 300 members
options.D: Senate with 120 members and House of Representatives with 360 members

questions.explanation: Nigeria's National Assembly is bicameral: the Senate has 109 members (3 per state + 1 for FCT) and the House of Representatives has 360 members allocated proportionally by population.

questions.stem: What was the NCNC's original full name at its founding?

options.B: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
options.D: Nigerian Citizens and Cameroons National Council

questions.explanation: When founded by Azikiwe in 1944, the NCNC stood for the National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons. It was later renamed the National Council of Nigerian Citizens after the Cameroons separated.

questions.stem: In what year did Nigeria's Northern Region gain self-governance?
questions.explanation: While the Eastern and Western Regions gained self-governance in 1957, the Northern Region only achieved self-governance in 1959, one year before Nigeria's full independence in 1960.

questions.stem: What was the fate of Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu, the leader of the January 1966 coup?

options.A: He fled to Ghana and died in exile in 1970
options.B: He was imprisoned by the Gowon regime and later killed during the Civil War on July 29, 1967
options.C: He was executed by firing squad alongside Dimka in 1976
options.D: He surrendered to Aguiyi-Ironsi and was later released

questions.explanation: Nzeogwu was imprisoned after the coup he led was co-opted by Aguiyi-Ironsi. After the Civil War began, he fought for Biafra and was killed on July 29, 1967 near Nsukka under circumstances that remain controversial.

questions.stem: Margaret Ekpo is notable in Nigerian history for what reason?

options.A: She was Nigeria's first female Head of State
options.B: She was one of Nigeria's first female political activists and an NCNC women's leader in the Eastern Region
options.C: She led the Aba Women's Riot of 1929
options.D: She was the first woman elected to the Nigerian Senate

questions.explanation: Margaret Ekpo was a pioneering female political figure in Nigeria, serving as a women's leader in the NCNC and an advocate for women's rights and inclusion in the political process in the Eastern Region.

questions.stem: What is Hamza AlMustapha known for in Nigerian history?

options.B: He was Abacha's Chief Security Officer, later convicted for the assassination of Kudirat Abiola
options.C: He was the EFCC chairman who prosecuted corrupt governors
options.D: He commanded Biafran forces at the Battle of Aba

questions.explanation: Major Hamza AlMustapha served as Chief Security Officer to General Sani Abacha and was later convicted for masterminding the assassination of Kudirat Abiola, MKO Abiola's wife, on June 4, 1996.

questions.stem: Who is the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism' buried at Lagos Island, and in what year did he die?
questions.explanation: Herbert Samuel Heelas Macaulay, regarded as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism,' died in 1945. He lived to see the formation of the NCNC, which he co-chaired with Azikiwe at the time of his death.

questions.stem: Which colonial governor's constitution imposed regionalism on Nigeria without Nigerian consultation?
questions.explanation: Governor Sir Arthur Richards introduced the Richards Constitution of 1946, which imposed regionalism on Nigeria without adequate consultation with Nigerian leaders, drawing widespread nationalist criticism.

questions.stem: What did Gowon's creation of 12 states in 1967 replace?

options.A: The 6-state structure from the Lyttleton Constitution
options.B: The 3-region structure introduced by the Richards Constitution
options.C: The 19-state structure created by Murtala Muhammed
options.D: The colonial district system of Lord Lugard

questions.explanation: Gowon's creation of 12 states in May 1967 replaced Nigeria's three-region structure (North, East, and West) that had been introduced by the Richards Constitution of 1946 and maintained since independence.

questions.stem: Which of Nigeria's civilian presidents died in office?
questions.explanation: President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua (2007-2010) is the only civilian president of Nigeria to die in office, passing away on May 5, 2010 from pericarditis and kidney complications.

questions.stem: What is MAMSER and under which regime was it established?

options.A: Mass Mobilisation for Agricultural Sector Recovery - Buhari regime
options.B: Mass Mobilisation for Social and Economic Recovery - IBB regime
options.C: Mass Movement for Social and Economic Reform - Abacha regime
options.D: Military Adjustment for Social and Economic Reconstruction - Gowon regime

questions.explanation: MAMSER (Mass Mobilisation for Social and Economic Recovery) was a civic re-orientation agency established under General Ibrahim Babangida's regime to promote participatory democracy and economic consciousness among Nigerians.

questions.stem: Who wrote the Nigerian national anthem currently in use, 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee'?
questions.explanation: The current Nigerian national anthem 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee' was written by Lillian Jean Williams, a British expatriate, and was restored as the national anthem in 2024.

questions.stem: What are the colours of the Nigerian national flag?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian national flag consists of two vertical green stripes on either side and a white stripe in the centre.

questions.stem: What do the green colours on the Nigerian flag represent?
questions.explanation: The two green stripes on the Nigerian flag symbolise the country's agricultural wealth and abundant natural resources.

questions.stem: What is the largest city in Nigeria by population?
questions.explanation: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria and one of the most populous cities in Africa, serving as the country's commercial capital.

questions.stem: Which flower appears on the Nigerian coat of arms?
questions.explanation: The Costus spectabilis, Nigeria's national flower, appears at the base of the Nigerian coat of arms.

questions.stem: What are Nigeria's two major religions?
questions.explanation: Christianity and Islam are the two dominant religions in Nigeria, with Islam predominant in the North and Christianity in the South.

questions.stem: Which river joins the River Niger in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The River Benue flows from Cameroon and joins the River Niger at Lokoja, Kogi State, forming the confluence from which the state derives its nickname.

questions.stem: What are Nigeria's three major ethnic groups?
questions.explanation: Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo are Nigeria's three largest and most prominent ethnic groups, dominating the North, South-West, and South-East respectively.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Treasure Base of the Nation'?
questions.explanation: Rivers State is called the 'Treasure Base of the Nation' due to its immense petroleum wealth and central role in Nigeria's oil and gas sector.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Centre of Unity'?
questions.explanation: Taraba State is called the 'Centre of Unity' due to the large number of diverse ethnic groups living together within its borders.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Land of Honour and Integrity'?
questions.explanation: Ekiti State is called the 'Land of Honour and Integrity,' reflecting the value its people place on education, culture, and principled conduct.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Heartbeat of the Nation'?
questions.explanation: Edo State is called the 'Heartbeat of the Nation,' a reference to its central location and rich cultural heritage, particularly the ancient Benin Kingdom.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Land of Promise'?
questions.explanation: Akwa Ibom State is nicknamed the 'Land of Promise,' reflecting its abundant oil wealth and agricultural potential.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Home of Peace and Tourism'?
questions.explanation: Cross River State is called the 'Home of Peace and Tourism' for its serene environment, wildlife, and the famous Calabar Carnival.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Confluence State'?
questions.explanation: Kogi State is known as the 'Confluence State' because the River Niger and River Benue meet (converge) at Lokoja, its capital city.

questions.stem: What does JAMB stand for?
questions.explanation: JAMB stands for Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, the Nigerian body responsible for conducting entrance examinations for tertiary institutions.

questions.stem: What does WAEC stand for?
questions.explanation: WAEC stands for the West African Examinations Council, the regional body responsible for conducting the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE).

questions.stem: What does NECO stand for?
questions.explanation: NECO stands for the National Examinations Council, the Nigerian body that conducts the National Senior Secondary Certificate Examination (NSSCE) for Nigerian secondary school students.

questions.stem: What does NAFDAC stand for?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.B: National Authority for Food and Drug Administration and Certification
options.C: Nigerian Agency for Food, Drugs and Consumer Control
options.D: National Agency for Food Distribution and Consumer Control

questions.explanation: NAFDAC stands for the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, responsible for regulating and controlling the manufacture, importation, exportation, sale, and distribution of food and drugs in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What does CBN stand for in the context of Nigerian institutions?
questions.explanation: CBN stands for the Central Bank of Nigeria, the country's apex monetary authority responsible for managing the naira, monetary policy, and financial system stability.

questions.stem: What does DSS stand for in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: DSS stands for the Department of State Services, Nigeria's internal intelligence and security agency responsible for gathering domestic intelligence and protecting national security.

questions.stem: What does FRSC stand for?
questions.explanation: FRSC stands for the Federal Road Safety Corps, the Nigerian agency responsible for administering road traffic laws, reducing road accidents, and issuing drivers' licences.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for appointing ministers in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Under the 1999 Constitution, the President of Nigeria is empowered to appoint ministers, subject to confirmation by the Senate.

questions.stem: Which body confirms ministerial appointments in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Senate is constitutionally empowered to screen and confirm ministerial nominees presented by the President before they can assume office.

questions.stem: Which state is credited with being the first to discover crude oil in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Oil was first discovered at Oloibiri in present-day Bayelsa State in 1956, marking the beginning of Nigeria's oil industry.

questions.stem: What is the Nigerian Police emergency contact number?
questions.explanation: 112 is Nigeria's unified emergency number for the police and can be dialled to report crimes or emergencies anywhere in the country.

questions.stem: Which state produces the most cocoa in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Ondo State is Nigeria's leading cocoa-producing state, contributing the largest share of Nigeria's cocoa exports and earning itself the title 'Sunshine State'.

questions.stem: Which state is most famous for oil production in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Rivers State, with Port Harcourt as its capital, is most commonly associated with oil production and is home to major petroleum industry infrastructure in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What is the subdivision of the Nigerian naira?
questions.explanation: The kobo is the subdivision of the Nigerian naira. One naira is divided into 100 kobo.

questions.stem: How many kobo make one naira?
questions.explanation: One Nigerian naira is equivalent to 100 kobo, the subdivided unit of Nigeria's national currency.

questions.stem: What is Nigeria's approximate population?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's population is estimated at over 230 million people, making it the most populous country in Africa and one of the most populous in the world.

questions.stem: Which ocean borders Nigeria to the south?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's southern coastline borders the Atlantic Ocean, specifically the Gulf of Guinea, which is part of the wider Atlantic Ocean.

questions.stem: Which specific body of water off Nigeria's southern coast is part of the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Guinea is the specific sea area of the Atlantic Ocean that borders Nigeria's southern coast, encompassing the Bight of Benin and Bight of Bonny.

questions.stem: How many countries are members of ECOWAS?
questions.explanation: ECOWAS currently has 15 member states, all located in West Africa.

questions.stem: Where is the headquarters of ECOWAS located?
questions.explanation: The headquarters of ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) is located in Abuja, Nigeria, reflecting Nigeria's dominant role in the organisation.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian university is popularly known by the abbreviation 'UI'?
questions.explanation: The University of Ibadan, Nigeria's oldest and most prestigious university, is commonly referred to by the abbreviation 'UI'.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian university is the largest by land mass?
questions.explanation: The University of Ilorin (UNILORIN) in Kwara State is the largest Nigerian university by land area, covering approximately 30,000 hectares.

questions.stem: What does NUC stand for?
questions.explanation: NUC stands for the National Universities Commission, the federal agency that regulates and accredits universities in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which body is responsible for regulating universities in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Universities Commission (NUC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating, accrediting, and overseeing university education in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which body is responsible for regulating polytechnics in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) regulates polytechnics, technical colleges, and other technical institutions in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What does NBTE stand for?
questions.explanation: NBTE stands for the National Board for Technical Education, the regulatory body for polytechnics and technical institutions in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which body is responsible for regulating colleges of education in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE) is responsible for regulating, accrediting, and overseeing colleges of education in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What does FIRS stand for?
questions.explanation: FIRS stands for the Federal Inland Revenue Service, Nigeria's apex tax authority responsible for collecting federal government taxes.

questions.stem: What does NCCE stand for in Nigerian education?

options.A: National Commission for Colleges of Education
options.C: Nigerian Committee for Curriculum and Examinations

questions.explanation: NCCE stands for the National Commission for Colleges of Education, the body that regulates and accredits colleges of education across Nigeria.

questions.stem: Who heads the Nigerian judiciary?

options.D: The President of the Court of Appeal

questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) heads the judiciary, presides over the Supreme Court, and is the highest judicial officer in the country.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Coal City State'?
questions.explanation: Enugu State is called the 'Coal City State' because of its rich coal deposits. The city of Enugu was developed around coal mining activities during the colonial era.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Fountain of Knowledge'?
questions.explanation: Osun State is nicknamed the 'Fountain of Knowledge' because of its high density of educational institutions and the historically literate Yoruba communities within it.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Salt of the Nation'?
questions.explanation: Ebonyi State is called the 'Salt of the Nation' due to its significant salt deposits and salt mining activities, particularly around the Uburu and Okposi lakes.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Land of Hospitality'?
questions.explanation: Benue State is nicknamed the 'Land of Hospitality' due to the warm, welcoming nature of its predominantly Tiv and Idoma people.

questions.stem: Which state is known as the 'Food Basket of the Nation'?
questions.explanation: Benue State is called the 'Food Basket of the Nation' because it is one of Nigeria's largest producers of food crops including yams, cassava, and sorghum.

questions.stem: What is the largest market in West Africa?
questions.explanation: The Onitsha Main Market in Anambra State is widely regarded as the largest market in West Africa by trading volume and the variety of goods it handles.

questions.stem: In which state is Onitsha, home of the largest market in West Africa, located?
questions.explanation: Onitsha is located in Anambra State, in south-eastern Nigeria. The city sits on the eastern bank of the River Niger.

questions.stem: What is Nigeria's time zone?
questions.explanation: Nigeria operates on West Africa Time (WAT), which is UTC+1, placing it one hour ahead of Greenwich Mean Time throughout the year.

questions.stem: What does WAT stand for in the context of Nigeria's time zone?
questions.explanation: WAT stands for West Africa Time, the standard time zone (UTC+1) used by Nigeria and several other West African nations.

questions.stem: How many countries does Nigeria share its borders with?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shares land borders with four countries: the Republic of Benin to the west, Niger to the north, Chad to the north-east, and Cameroon to the east.

questions.stem: Which countries share borders with Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's land borders are shared with: the Republic of Benin (west), Niger Republic (north), Republic of Chad (north-east), and Republic of Cameroon (east).

questions.stem: What is the first line of the Nigerian National Pledge?

options.A: I pledge to Nigeria my country
options.C: I pledge to serve my country Nigeria
options.D: I pledge to be a faithful Nigerian

questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Pledge begins with 'I pledge to Nigeria my country,' followed by pledges of faithfulness, honesty, and service to the nation.

questions.stem: Which body is responsible for printing and issuing the Nigerian currency?
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is solely responsible for issuing legal tender currency in Nigeria, overseeing the printing and minting of naira notes and coins.

questions.stem: Which ministry is responsible for overseeing education in Nigeria at the federal level?
questions.explanation: The Federal Ministry of Education is responsible for formulating and implementing educational policies and overseeing Nigeria's educational sector at the national level.

questions.stem: Which ministry is responsible for overseeing health matters at the federal level in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Federal Ministry of Health is responsible for formulating national health policies, regulating healthcare delivery, and overseeing public health matters in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which federal body is responsible for collecting taxes on behalf of the Nigerian government?
questions.explanation: The Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) is responsible for assessing, collecting, and accounting for all taxes and levies due to the Federal Government of Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which agency in Nigeria is responsible for handling immigration matters?

options.D: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons

questions.explanation: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) is the federal agency responsible for managing immigration, border control, and the regulation of travel documents in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which agency is responsible for issuing passports in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Immigration Service is responsible for issuing international passports, visas, and residence permits to Nigerian citizens and foreign nationals.

questions.stem: Which body handles customs and import/export duties in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) is the federal agency responsible for assessing and collecting import and export duties, and for controlling the movement of goods across Nigeria's borders.

questions.stem: Which body is responsible for managing Nigeria's airports?
questions.explanation: The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) is responsible for the management, operation, and maintenance of all international and domestic airports in Nigeria.

questions.stem: What does FAAN stand for?
questions.explanation: FAAN stands for the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, the government agency that manages and develops airports across the country.

questions.stem: Which airport is Nigeria's busiest international airport?
questions.explanation: Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) in Lagos is Nigeria's busiest airport, handling the majority of international and domestic air traffic in the country.

questions.stem: What is Nigeria's largest seaport?
questions.explanation: Lagos Port (also known as Apapa Port) is Nigeria's largest and busiest seaport, handling the bulk of the country's maritime imports and exports.

questions.stem: What is the international currency code for the Nigerian naira?
questions.explanation: NGN is the ISO 4217 currency code for the Nigerian naira, used in international financial transactions and foreign exchange markets.

questions.stem: Which type of institution in Nigeria is primarily responsible for training teachers?
questions.explanation: Colleges of Education in Nigeria are specifically established to train teachers for primary and junior secondary schools, awarding the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE).

questions.stem: What does TETFUND stand for?
questions.explanation: TETFUND stands for the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, a Nigerian intervention agency established to provide supplementary funding to public tertiary educational institutions.

questions.stem: What does NIMC stand for?
questions.explanation: NIMC stands for the National Identity Management Commission, the Nigerian agency responsible for establishing and managing the national identity database and issuing National Identification Numbers.

questions.stem: Which document does the NIMC issue to Nigerian citizens and residents?
questions.explanation: The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) issues the National Identification Number (NIN), a unique 11-digit number assigned to each Nigerian citizen and legal resident.

questions.stem: What does NIN stand for?
questions.explanation: NIN stands for National Identification Number, the unique 11-digit number issued by the NIMC to identify every Nigerian citizen and legal resident in the national database.

questions.stem: Which body regulates the telecommunications industry in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) is the independent regulatory authority for the telecommunications industry in Nigeria, overseeing mobile networks, internet service providers, and related services.

questions.stem: What does NCC stand for in the context of Nigerian government agencies?
questions.explanation: NCC stands for the Nigerian Communications Commission, the regulatory body for the telecommunications sector in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which body regulates broadcasting in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) is responsible for regulating and controlling the activities of all broadcasting stations in Nigeria, including television and radio.

questions.stem: What does NBC stand for in the context of Nigerian regulatory agencies?
questions.explanation: NBC stands for the National Broadcasting Commission, the body that regulates broadcasting content and licences radio and television stations in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which body manages Nigeria's stock exchange?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), formerly the Nigerian Stock Exchange (NSE), is the body that manages Nigeria's main stock exchange where shares and securities are bought and sold.

questions.stem: What is the abbreviation for the Nigerian Exchange Group?
questions.explanation: NGX is the official abbreviation for the Nigerian Exchange Group, the holding company for Nigeria's main securities exchange.

questions.stem: Which crop is Nigeria most famous for exporting after crude oil?
questions.explanation: Cocoa is Nigeria's most significant non-oil agricultural export, and Nigeria was once the world's largest cocoa producer before the oil boom shifted focus away from agriculture.

questions.stem: On which continent is Nigeria located?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is located in West Africa on the African continent, bordered by the Gulf of Guinea to the south and sharing land borders with Benin, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon.

questions.stem: What is the slogan of Lagos State?
questions.explanation: Lagos State is nicknamed the 'Centre of Excellence,' reflecting its status as Nigeria's commercial, financial, and cultural hub.

questions.stem: Why were the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria amalgamated in 1914?

options.A: To unite them for easy administration and economic efficiency
options.B: To satisfy the demands of Nigerian nationalists
options.C: To prepare Nigeria for immediate independence
options.D: To create a single military force for West Africa

questions.explanation: The 1914 amalgamation was driven by British colonial interests in achieving easier administrative control and greater economic efficiency across the two protectorates.

questions.stem: A form of marriage in which a person marries within the same ethnic group, religion, clan, or social class is called __________.
questions.explanation: Endogamy is the practice of marrying within a specific social group, community, or class, as required by custom or law.

questions.stem: A form of marriage in which a person marries outside their own ethnic group, clan, or social group is called __________.
questions.explanation: Exogamy is the social practice of marrying outside one's own social group, community, or clan.

questions.stem: Nigeria operates which system of government?
questions.explanation: Nigeria operates a federal system of government in which powers are divided between the central (federal) government and the constituent state governments.

questions.stem: The number of states in Nigeria is __________.
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 36 states in addition to the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja.

questions.stem: The legislative arm at the federal level in Nigeria is known as the __________.
questions.explanation: The National Assembly is the bicameral federal legislature of Nigeria, consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an element of culture?
questions.explanation: Genetics is a biological inheritance, not a cultural element. Culture consists of learned behaviours, beliefs, and practices - not biological traits.

questions.stem: Cultural transmission occurs through __________.
questions.explanation: Culture is passed from one generation to the next through the processes of learning and socialization, not through biological means.

questions.stem: Cultural relativism means __________.

options.B: Judging culture by your own standards

questions.explanation: Cultural relativism is the principle that a person's beliefs and activities should be understood based on that person's own culture, and no culture should be judged as superior or inferior.

questions.stem: Nigerian society is best described as __________.
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a heterogeneous society comprising over 250 ethnic groups, multiple languages, religions, and cultural practices, making it highly diverse.

questions.stem: The smallest unit of society is the __________.
questions.explanation: The family is universally recognized as the smallest and most fundamental unit of any society, forming the foundation for social organization.

questions.stem: Bride price is most associated with which type of marriage?
questions.explanation: Bride price (or bride wealth) is a key feature of traditional African marriage, paid by the groom's family to the bride's family as part of customary marriage rites.

questions.stem: African traditional religion recognizes __________.
questions.explanation: African traditional religion is not atheistic or polytheistic in the absolute sense - it acknowledges one Supreme Being (God) above all other divinities and spirits.

questions.stem: The intermediaries between God and humans in African religion are __________.
questions.explanation: In African traditional religion, divinities, spirits, ancestors, and religious specialists (priests) serve as intermediaries between the Supreme Being and ordinary humans.

questions.stem: Divination is used in African religion to __________.
questions.explanation: Divination is a ritual practice used in African traditional religion to seek knowledge, communicate with the spirit world, and receive guidance from divinities or ancestors.

questions.stem: Ancestors in African belief are thought to __________.

options.C: Have no role in community life
options.D: Be ordinary humans with no influence

questions.explanation: In African traditional belief, ancestors do not simply cease to exist after death; they are believed to continue living in the spirit world and actively participating in the affairs of the living.

questions.stem: Sacred places in African traditional religion include __________.
questions.explanation: In African traditional religion, natural features such as rivers, forests, hills, and certain trees are considered sacred because they are believed to be inhabited by spiritual forces.

questions.stem: Totems in African culture are __________.
questions.explanation: Totems are sacred symbols, plants, or animals that serve as emblems for clans, families, or individuals in African communities, often believed to have a spiritual or protective relationship with the group.

questions.stem: The image of the horse in the Nigerian coat of arms symbolizes __________.
questions.explanation: The two white horses (eagles) supporting the shield on the Nigerian coat of arms represent the dignity of the Nigerian nation.

questions.stem: The currency note that reflects the major ethnic groups in Nigeria is the __________.
questions.explanation: The N50 note features images representing Nigeria's diverse ethnic nationalities, making it the currency note most associated with ethnic representation.

questions.stem: A condition whereby only persons of royal blood can become Head of State is called __________.
questions.explanation: A monarchy is a system of government in which the position of head of state is inherited through royal lineage and is typically held for life.

questions.stem: A constitution means __________.

options.A: All of the above - an agreed set of rules, fundamental laws of a state, and rules governing sovereign power
options.B: Only an agreed set of rules for organizing government
options.C: Only the philosophy and fundamental laws of a state
options.D: Only rules affecting the distribution of sovereign power

questions.explanation: A constitution comprehensively embodies all three: an agreed set of rules for government organization, the philosophy and fundamental laws of a state, and the rules governing the exercise of sovereign power.

questions.stem: The name Nigeria was derived from the River Niger, which is the __________ largest river in Africa.
questions.explanation: The River Niger is the third longest river in Africa, after the Nile and the Congo, and gave Nigeria its name.

questions.stem: The major problem of Nigeria today is widely considered to be __________.
questions.explanation: Corruption is the most widely cited fundamental challenge to Nigeria's development, affecting governance, the economy, and public institutions at all levels.

questions.stem: Production of arts and crafts such as leather work, weaving, and carving are categorized under which traditional economic activities?
questions.explanation: The production of crafts like leather goods, woven fabrics, and carvings involves processing raw materials into finished goods, which places them in the secondary sector of economic activity.

questions.stem: The following are among the conditions for siting a traditional settlement EXCEPT __________.
questions.explanation: Traditional settlements were located based on natural factors such as water supply, fertile soil, and available building land. Internet connectivity is a modern requirement that did not exist when traditional settlements were established.

questions.stem: One means of traditional capital formation is __________.

options.B: Taking a loan from a bank
options.C: Buying shares from the stock exchange

questions.explanation: 'Oju-Oto' is a traditional Nigerian system of informal savings where individuals accumulate funds over time, representing a pre-modern form of capital formation outside the formal banking sector.

questions.stem: Nationalism in Nigeria was greatly influenced by __________.
questions.explanation: Cultural nationalism - expressed through socio-cultural organisations like Egbe Omo Oduduwa and Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa - significantly fuelled the Nigerian nationalist movement and the drive for independence.

questions.stem: The Action Group was formed from the __________ socio-cultural organization.
questions.explanation: The Action Group (AG), founded by Chief Obafemi Awolowo in 1951, grew out of the Yoruba cultural and social organisation Egbe Omo Oduduwa.

questions.stem: The Northern People's Congress (NPC) was formed from which cultural organization?
questions.explanation: The NPC emerged from the socio-cultural organization Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa, which literally means 'Association of the People of the North.'

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a symbol of national identity in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The national flag, coat of arms, national anthem, and national pledge are all official national symbols. 'National prints' is not a recognized category of national identity symbols.

questions.stem: The organization that oversees the declaration of assets by public officials in Nigeria is the __________.
questions.explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau is the Nigerian government body constitutionally mandated to receive and examine asset declarations made by public officers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a formal source of the Nigerian constitution?
questions.explanation: Customs, norms, and taboos can inform constitutional principles through their role in shaping social values, but personal biographies are not recognized as formal sources of constitutional law.

questions.stem: One major advantage of a written constitution is that __________.

options.A: The document serves as an easy reference book for law courts
options.B: It can degenerate into a dictatorship
options.C: The process of amendment can be financially tasking

questions.explanation: A key advantage of a written constitution is its accessibility - courts, citizens, and officials can easily refer to the single document to understand the fundamental law of the land.

questions.stem: Within a democracy, citizens __________.

options.A: Have the right and duty to be involved in the political process
options.B: Can use all means to overthrow an offensive government
options.C: Have the duty to eliminate their political opponents

questions.explanation: Democracy is a system of government where citizens have both the right and the responsibility to participate actively in political processes, including voting and engaging with governance.

questions.stem: The constitution of any given country must provide for __________.

options.A: All of the above: distribution of powers, rule of law, and rights and duties of individuals
options.D: The rights and duties of individuals only

questions.explanation: A complete constitution must address all three: how governmental powers are distributed, the supremacy of law, and the fundamental rights and corresponding duties of every citizen.

questions.stem: The basic economic problems which man aims at solving through economic activities include all of the following EXCEPT __________.

options.C: How much of these goods should be produced

questions.explanation: The three classic economic problems are: what to produce, how much to produce, and for whom to produce. The question of where to sell is a marketing decision, not one of the fundamental economic problems.
